The prompts are revised and the scene regenerated until the uncanny valley is hopefully bridged.double quotation markIt becomes a case of treating the model like a marionette doll and tweaking individual stringsWhere, say, Klaus Kinski could summon torrents of rage by tapping into his personal demons, an AI programmer has to achieve the same effect in much more approximate ways. “An AI is not an actor, so how do you communicate the internal state of a character?” says Zack London, who asGossip Goblinmakes highly baroque AI-generated sci-fi shorts. “You can say: they look confused, or they say this in jest, or they say this sternly. But it’s such a broad stroke. The model will probably come out with a very over-the-top telenovela-type performance, or will just not understand.” At that point, it becomes a case of treating the model like a “marionette doll” and tweaking individual strings. “You could say: there’s a slight quiver on the left side of their lip, and then their gaze diverts slightly downwards, and they look up again and blink.”London chooses to keep a human ghost in the machine by first recording dialogue with real actors, around which he retro-fits the animation. He is candid about the shortcomings of the current prompting process, saying the results suit a certain type of film: “The acting is not going to be particularly subtle, like some grand Anthony Hopkins or Olivia Colman performance. It’s more like an old-school Terry Gilliam or Guy Ritchie performance, where the characters are larger than life.” But maybe that’s where the danger lies for actors: many blockbuster performances, meting out simple beats of easily comprehensible emotion, have a cut-and-paste quality – and are therefore susceptible to AI.Then again, a mundane magic still happens even on blockbuster sets. “Sometimes the most brilliant moment happens in the fraction of a second. And you can’t put your finger on why an actor gives a certain look,” saysTye Sheridan, the co-founder (in 2016) of Wonder Dynamics, an Autodesk company who developed the AI production tool Autodesk Flow Studio. He should know: he was the star of Steven Spielberg’s 2018 filmReady Player One, which itself patrolled the frontier between real and digital.View image in fullscreen‘You can’t put your finger on it’ … Tye Sheridan in Ready Player One.Photograph: courtesy of Warner Bros Pictures/APSheridan shares Higgsfield’s belief that AI-driven methods can democratise film-making. But he is adamant that performances should retain a human core.Flow Studiouses AI for an augmented and far cheaper version of motion capture, layering CG characters and environments on top of filmed footage. At Framestore, Webber is exploring similar AI tools that allow him to apply what he calls “digital makeup” to traditional performances, without the guesswork involved in generative prompts.He, London and Sheridan agree that this hybrid form of film-making still allows actors to make specific choices essential to authentic creation. “You have to ask, with these generative models: are they really designed to deliver legendary performances, or are they designed to cut to an average?” asks Sheridan. Alimzhanov, though, insists something akin to an actor’s internal process is achievable via AI. The prompting used on The Cully Hill Boys was different in one key regard: instead of replicating emotions by specifying the physical mechanics, the AI model generated sequences based on contextual input about what the characters were experiencing.These two camps of AI acting – technological and human-centric – are fighting the latest bout in the struggle between the forces that have shaped the craft: external v internal; reproducing v experiencing; Laurence Olivier telling Dustin Hoffman that, instead of staying awake for 72 hours, he should “try acting, dear boy”. But where Stanislavsky promoted the internal quest to revitalise acting, this could be the first time in the modern era when the formalist approach – the mannered reproduction of emotions – looks like the future.Opening the digital floodgates could lead toWilliam Gibson territory, where deathless virtual stars seduce the masses, as in his 1996 novel Idoru. But it’s still not clear whether the box office demand, and thus a true economic case, for AI cinema exists. And we’re yet to see a compelling script that crystallises the possibilities of the tech in story form, as The Matrix did for CGI. If we’re inundated with unloved AI abominations, the words of Val Kilmer in Tombstone, playing that icon of human mortality, Doc Holliday, will ring anew: “There’s just something about him. Something around the eyes reminds me of … me. I’m sure of it – I hate him.”Explore more on these topicsFilmAI (artificial intelligence)Val KilmerTilly Norwood (AI character)featuresShareReuse this content

title: Billionaire Mukesh Ambani launches India’s biggest-ever IPO | IPOs | The Guardian
description: Low-cost broadband provider Jio Platforms aims for £81bn valuation when it floats on the stock market on Wednesday
Author: Julia Kollewe
Headline: Low-cost broadband provider Jio Platforms aims for £81bn valuation when it floats on the stock market on Wednesday
Content: Mukesh Ambani, chairman and managing director of Reliance Industries.Photograph: Amit Dave/ReutersView image in fullscreenMukesh Ambani, chairman and managing director of Reliance Industries.Photograph: Amit Dave/ReutersIPOsBillionaire Mukesh Ambani launches India’s biggest-ever IPOLow-cost broadband provider Jio Platforms aims for £81bn valuation when it floats on the stock market on WednesdayJulia KolleweTue 20 Oct 2026 05.53 EDTLast modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 18.57 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIndia’s second-richest man, Mukesh Ambani, is launching what could be the country’s biggest-ever initial public offering (IPO), despite a stock market downturn.Mumbai-based Jio Platforms, a telecoms company backed by Meta Platforms and Google, is hoping to raise up to 302bn rupees (£2.4bn) and is targeting a 10.3tn rupees valuation when it floats on the stock market from Wednesday.Set up a decade ago as a subsidiary of Ambani’s conglomerate Reliance Industries, and led by Akash Ambani, the oldest son of patriarch Mukesh, Jio offers low-cost broadband to millions of Indians.Indian billionaire’s payments firm plots biggest London flotation in yearsRead moreJio secured 212 anchor investors on Monday before its blockbuster IPO. They include some of the world’s largest fund managers, such as: BlackRock; Singapore’s sovereign wealth fund; the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority; Fidelity Investments; Schroders; JP Morgan Asset Management; Franklin Templeton; Invesco; and Prudential.On Wednesday, shares will be offered to retail investors, and the IPO is set to close on Friday.Reliance Industries said in a stock exchangefilinglast week that Jio had set a price range of 1,065 rupees to 1,119 rupees a share for its maiden share sale, offering up to 270m new shares.The family-owned conglomerate has been encouraging its 400,000-plus employees to buy shares, offering them a discount of 54 rupees a share.At the top end of the price range, Jio would be worth 10.3tn rupees, which would make it India’s fourth-largest company, behind its parent Reliance Industries, Bharti Airtel and HDFC Bank. It would be more than twice as much as the 4.9tn-rupee valuation in 2020, when Meta and Google invested in the company.However, the top valuation is far below initial expectations of more than £110bn when the telecoms group posted a draft prospectus in the summer.It comes amid a broader stock market slowdown in India, with the blue chip Nifty 5o index down more than 12% this year.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThis is IndiaNiha Masih takes a look at the stories, ideas and news makers of modern IndiaEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionJio launched its telecoms services in September 2016. It gained 16 million subscribers in the first month, and topped 100 million subscribers within 170 days, according to Reliance Industries. It is credited with making mobile internet more affordable, by triggering a price war. The company intends to expand further into artificial intelligence, cloud computing and digital infrastructure.Isha Ambani, who sits on Jio’s board as a director,told investors last weekthat the business idea was spawned by the poor connectivity she and her brother Akash faced when they returned to India on a break from studying in the US in about 2009-10. She struggled to submit a college assignment online because the internet was not working.“What followed was a conversation about why should India be left behind,” she said. “Akash firmly believed that the answer and solution to this was creating a digital technology platform company.”Explore more on these topicsIPOsIndiaSouth and central AsiaStock marketsInternet IPOsTelecommunications industryISPsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Mac Allister double sparks Liverpool’s thrilling comeback win over Villarreal | Champions League | The Guardian
description: Ronald Araújo and Florian Wirtz were also on target as Liverpool hit back from 2-0 down to stun Villarreal 4-3 in the Champions League
Author: Andy Hunter
Headline: Ronald Araújo and Florian Wirtz were also on target as Liverpool hit back from 2-0 down to stun Villarreal 4-3 in the Champions League
Content: Alexis Mac Allister (left) hugs Kostas Tsimikas after giving Liverpool the lead with his second goal of the night.Photograph: Ryan Browne/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenAlexis Mac Allister (left) hugs Kostas Tsimikas after giving Liverpool the lead with his second goal of the night.Photograph: Ryan Browne/ShutterstockChampions LeagueMac Allister double sparks Liverpool’s thrilling comeback win over VillarrealAndy Hunterat AnfieldTue 20 Oct 2026 17.04 EDTLast modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 18.55 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAndoni Iraola and Iñigo Pérez parked a long and close friendship in the buildup to their first competitive confrontation as coaches. The old Athletic Bilbao teammates will have a humdinger of aChampions Leaguecontest to dissect once communications are restored. Liverpool, ignited by Rio Ngumoha, recovered from two goals down against Villarreal to maintain their 100% record plus their gathering momentum.Alexis Mac Allister struck twice, Florian Wirtz capped recent improvement with his first goal of the season while Liverpool were dreadful for the opening 30 minutes, transformed after the break and fretting in stoppage time after Tani Oluwaseyi had volleyed in a third forVillarreal. The game flipped on Sergi Cardona’s mistake and Ronald Araújo’s equaliser with the final touch of the first half. “We weren’t able to handle the emotion tonight,” conceded Villarreal coach Pérez.Doué and Vitinha burn bright as brittle Barcelona come unstuck against PSGRead moreBut the lasting impression was of Ngumoha seizing responsibility in the absence of big names and drivingLiverpoolon at the age of 18. The winger was electric, the difference maker, and from the right-wing role that he is still adapting to. He supplied the cross for Araújo’s all-important leveller and unravelled the Villarreal defence for Mac Allister’s second, Liverpool’s third on a rollercoaster of a night and performance.“Rio didn’t have it easy tonight,” said Iraola. “They demanded a lot of him defensively with their left-back attacking but he was very difficult to stop. If you can put him in one-v-ones he can make space and produce things, like the lovely assist for Alexis, and endurance-wise he is able to play more and more minutes. He is eager to improve and if he can add things to his game he’ll become the full package.”The regular phone calls between Iraola and Pérez had ceased in the days leading up to the fixture. Had they continued the Liverpool head coach might have told his opposite number to bring a coat and not wear a short-sleeved polo shirt on a day of incessant rain. Iraola rested Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola. A fourth game in 10 days explained the omissions of Wirtz and Barcola, who had featured heavily in the previous three, while Isak’s workload was being carefully managed after his recent thigh injury.Liverpool’s much-changed team fell behind quickly. An error-strewn start by Virgil van Dijk was responsible, and also in keeping with a ponderous opening half hour from the hosts. Villarreal passed their way around Anfield with style and precious little resistance.The Liverpool captain presented Georges Mikautadze with an immediate opportunity when he misjudged a long clearance by Renato Veiga. Van Dijk’s poor touch almost released the Georgia international striker through on goal but Jérémy Jacquet closed off that route. Van Dijk’s second slip followed moments later, and this time there was no reprieve. The defender attempted to head another Veiga long ball back into the safe arms of Alisson. He found Mikautadze instead and Villarreal’s No 9 pounced expertly, controlling well before rolling the ball under the Liverpool keeper. There were apologies all round from Van Dijk.View image in fullscreenAlexis Mac Allister heads home to score Liverpool’s opening goal.Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Ed Sykes/Apl/SportsphotoVillarreal doubled their lead with a goal that encapsulated the start made by both teams – the visitors passing their way through Liverpool’s midfield and picking holes in their high defensive line, with the home side slow to react. Pape Gueye, Alberto Moleiro and Nathan Saliba combined to send their rampaging left-back, Cardona, through on goal. Played onside by Kostas Tsimikas, the full-back beat Alisson with a finish a striker would have been proud of.Cardona’s defending was much less impressive as Liverpool clawed their way back into the contest. The recovery commenced when Mac Allister rose superbly to meet a Tsimikas corner and flicked an unstoppable header into the unguarded side of Peter Gulacsi’s goal.Villarreal’s comfort vanished entirely when Ngumoha clipped a cross towards the far post following another Tsimikas corner. Cardona checked his surroundings, then inexplicably let the ball bounce behind him, and right into the spot where Araújo was lurking. The on-loan defender headed home for the second successive week in the Champions League and celebrated with a mass pile-on with fans in the Anfield Road Stand.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAraújo was withdrawn at the interval because Iraola felt Liverpool would match up better to Villarreal with Ryan Gravenberch at right-back and Wirtz restored to the forward line. And so it proved. Liverpool improved vastly after the restart with Ngumoha and Wirtz a constant, marauding threat.View image in fullscreenRonald Araújo heads home Liverpool’s second goal in first-half stoppage time.Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/ReutersNgumoha took the acclaim of the Kop after creating Mac Allister’s second of the night with a sparkling run down the right. It was some one-two that brought Liverpool the lead. Mac Allister floated a pass out to the winger, whose first touch brought the ball under control and took him away from Cardona in the same movement. He then left the substitute Juan Foyth in his wake before pulling back a pass from the byline for the incoming midfielder to smash a shot in off the underside of Gulacsi’s crossbar.Wirtz completed the comeback after Tsimikas and Cody Gakpo had combined to create space for the playmaker inside the area. The Germany international drilled a clinical left-footed finish inside the Villarreal keeper’s far corner. Oluwaseyi created a nervous finale when converting a cross from the former Newcastle forward Ayoze Pérez but Liverpool held firm. “We started too relaxed and we were too relaxed at 4-2,” Iraola said. “But against a really good Villarreal team I give value and importance to this win.”Explore more on these topicsChampions LeagueLiverpoolVillarrealEuropean club footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Robinson sparks 23-0 run as Pistons stun Celtics in NBA season opener | NBA | The Guardian
description: Duncan Robinson inspired a stunning fourth-quarter comeback as Detroit overturned a 22-point deficit to beat Boston 121-113 in the NBA season opener
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Duncan Robinson inspired a stunning fourth-quarter comeback as Detroit overturned a 22-point deficit to beat Boston 121-113 in the NBA season opener
Content: Detroit Pistons forward Duncan Robinson shoots over Boston Celtics guard Derrick White during the second half of Tuesday’s NBA season opener in Detroit.Photograph: Paul Sancya/APView image in fullscreenDetroit Pistons forward Duncan Robinson shoots over Boston Celtics guard Derrick White during the second half of Tuesday’s NBA season opener in Detroit.Photograph: Paul Sancya/APNBARobinson sparks 23-0 run as Pistons stun Celtics in NBA season openerDetroit erase 22-point deficit to beat Boston 121-113Paul George scores 38 points on Celtics debut in defeatRobinson scores 15 of his 21 points in fourth quarterAgenciesTue 20 Oct 2026 18.35 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleDuncan Robinson scored 15 of his 21 points in the fourth quarter as theDetroit Pistonsreeled off 23 unanswered points to beat the visiting Boston Celtics 121-113 in the NBA’s regular-season opener on Tuesday afternoon.Jalen Duren and Cade Cunningham scored 22 points apiece for the Pistons, who led the Eastern Conference with 60 wins last season.Javonte Green came off the bench to score 19 points in 18 minutes, while Ausar Thompson added 11 points, 11 rebounds and five assists.NBA 2026-27 season predictions: A Knicks repeat and LeBron’s villain arcRead morePaul George scored a game-high 38 points on his Celtics debut. Payton Pritchard and Derrick White scored 17 points apiece, but Jayson Tatum was held to 13 points on six-for-23 shooting, although he contributed 11 assists.The Celtics led by 13 at halftime thanks to a second-quarter surge. Detroit held a 39-35 advantage early in the quarter before Boston reeled off 15 unanswered points.George scored the Celtics’ final eight points of the half as Boston took a 58-45 lead into the break.George showed no signs of cooling off in the third quarter, hitting three three-pointers in a 52-second span to give Boston their biggest lead at 72-50.Green entered the game shortly afterward to slow George down. He not only did that but also gave Detroit an offensive spark, scoring 11 points in the quarter, including three three-pointers, as the Pistons pulled within three in the closing seconds.George opened the fourth quarter with a layup to give Boston a 90-82 lead. The Celtics soon stretched their advantage to 12 points, but Detroit began another comeback, sparked by a three-point play from Thompson.Robinson scored 11 straight points to pull the Pistons within one at 99-98. He then set up a three-pointer for Green before Duren converted a three-point play. Robinson hit another three-pointer with 5min 13sec remaining to put Detroit ahead 107-99.Green capped the 23-0 run with another three-pointer, extending the Pistons’ lead to 112-99 with 3min 33sec left.Boston rallied to within four points, but Green made two free throws with 6.7 seconds remaining to seal Detroit’s opening-day victory.Explore more on these topicsNBADetroit PistonsBoston CelticsBasketballUS sportsShareReuse this content

title: Foden hat-trick helps Manchester City cut through noise and crush AEK Athens | Champions League | The Guardian
description: Manchester City thumped AEK Athens 5-1, Phil Foden scoring a hat-trick as the hosts got their Champions League campaign back on track
Author: Will Unwin
Headline: Manchester City thumped AEK Athens 5-1, Phil Foden scoring a hat-trick as the hosts got their Champions League campaign back on track
Content: Phil Foden races away after scoring the first of his three goals against AEK Athens.Photograph: Mike Egerton/PAView image in fullscreenPhil Foden races away after scoring the first of his three goals against AEK Athens.Photograph: Mike Egerton/PAChampions LeagueFoden hat-trick helps Manchester City cut through noise and crush AEK AthensWill Unwinat the Etihad StadiumTue 20 Oct 2026 17.00 EDTLast modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 21.14 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GooglePhil Foden shouted the loudest on a quiet night at the Etihad Stadium, announcing his personal return to form with an instinctive hat-trick as Manchester City dispatched AEK Athens with little fuss. Enzo Maresca had called for City to make their own noise amid the cacophony around the club but a businesslike victory in front of 20,000 fewer than watched the weekend’swin over Ipswichwas required to get their Champions League back on track after sufferingat the hands of Paris Saint-Germain.Those in attendance, officially 40,042 but that felt optimistic, saw Foden shine on the right wing and as a central striker, showing there is life without Erling Haaland, who watched from the bench. Admittedly, the opposition were not a match for the Premier League side, whose other goals came from Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki. Stavros Pilios’s consolation was more a reward for the boisterous fans in yellow and black, who created the atmosphere, than for the overall efforts of the visitors.Doué and Vitinha burn bright as brittle Barcelona come unstuck against PSGRead moreFoden has endured a difficult time; Saturday’s goal was his first since mid-December. He has spent much of the season watching on from the sidelines, some of that absence self-inflicted after getting sent off for kicking out in frustrationin the Manchester derby. He was tightly wound at that point but there is a growing freedom to his game, flitting between roles when required with devastating effect.“Slowly but surely,” Foden said of getting back to his best. “Still got a long way to go, but I am going in the right direction. Scoring along the way definitely helps. I want to keep working hard and keep being the best I can for the manager and the team. When I changed into that false 9 role, I enjoyed it a lot. Really enjoyed that role tonight.”View image in fullscreenPhil Foden scores the fourth goal with a sublime first-time finish.Photograph: Peter Powell/EPAMaresca took the calculated risk of eight changes, although that did mean a return to the starting lineup for Enzo Fernández and Anderson while Haaland was only there in case of emergency. His replacement, with senior options lacking, was the 17-year-old academy graduate, Floyd Samba, whose only other senior football came in a Carabao Cup win against Norwich,when he scored twice on debut.The game had not captured the imagination with the stands having huge gaps of blue, which is understandable amid the constant churn of fixtures for City and the cost of following the club. AEK was seen by many fans as a game that could be missed, in expectation of a simple victory over a team lacking global superstars. The visiting supporters were far more animated, filling a corner of the ground over three tiers where they created a party from two hours before kick-off. “Our fans are amazing,” Marko Nikolic, the AEK head coach, said.Inspiration was required from those on the pitch with the home faithful subdued, and it was provided in the 12th minute by Fernández clipping a free-kick on to the bar. Anderson followed up to whack the rebound into an empty net. The celebrations lacked enthusiasm, acknowledged with a nod of approval.View image in fullscreenElliot Anderson fires Manchester City ahead from close range.Photograph: Scott Heppell/ReutersAEK did what they could to resist but City were able to take control, passing the ball around with ease and holding AEK at arm’s length, while Foden and Cherki tried to work their fleet-footed magic in tight spaces. Eventually the calmness in the final third was rewarded when Foden finished after neat work on the right from Rico Lewis, as the two academy products combined. The full-back has struggled for minutes in recent times and almost left the club 16 months ago but showed he can provide something as an attacking threat from defence.Pilios thrashed home but natural order was soon restored by Cherki, a neat trick inside the box and a precise shot into the corner did the rest. It was an occasion for the maverick Frenchman to be a leader, making the difference in critical moments and he offered evidence of his capabilities with the finish, creating breathing space in the process.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionIf the plan was to test life without Haaland, the loss of Antoine Semenyo to injury for eight weeks created a problem for Maresca. Samba’s deployment ranked somewhere between plan C and D but the teenager was an adept decoy, allowing the more experienced around him to show off their repertoire.City started to showboat as AEK realised resistance was futile. Cherki knocked it long for Lewis to control into the path of Foden, who provided a sublime first-time finish into the top corner from the edge of the box. The exceptional goals were racking up on what felt like an otherwise mundane night.View image in fullscreenRayan Cherki (second left) restores Manchester City’s two-goal advantage.Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAOn a positive night for City’s academy, Ryan McAidoo came off the bench to send in a perfect cross for Foden to complete his treble with a striker’s instinct, earning the biggest cheer of the night. Being able to celebrate one of their own is important for City fans, especially with so many unknowns.“I consider him one of the best English players but for different reasons in the last two-three years, he was not good enough – but I know how good he is,” Maresca said. “We are just trying to help him because we are sure that he’s going to help us this season.”Explore more on these topicsChampions LeagueManchester CityAEK AthensEuropean club footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: NFL will not discipline Eagles over handling of Jalen Hurts’ blood clots | Philadelphia Eagles | The Guardian
description: NFL says it coordinated with Philadelphia’s medical staff over the quarterback’s treatment before he was diagnosed with blood clots in his lungs
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: NFL says it coordinated with Philadelphia’s medical staff over the quarterback’s treatment before he was diagnosed with blood clots in his lungs
Content: Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts during the NFL game against the Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London on 11 October.Photograph: Manjit Narotra/ProSports/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenEagles quarterback Jalen Hurts during the NFL game against the Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London on 11 October.Photograph: Manjit Narotra/ProSports/ShutterstockPhiladelphia EaglesNFL will not discipline Eagles over handling of Jalen Hurts’ blood clotsLeague consulted with Eagles doctors over treatmentHurts played in London after initial clot diagnosisQuarterback expected to miss rest of NFL seasonAssociated PressTue 20 Oct 2026 16.51 EDTLast modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 16.52 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThePhiladelphia Eagleswill not face disciplinary action over their handling of quarterback Jalen Hurts’ blood clots, according to a person familiar with the situation.The person spoke to the Associated Press on condition of anonymity Tuesday because conversations between the league and the team were to remain private.Jalen Hurts played through a blood clot. Are NFL players cattle?Read moreIn a statement released Tuesday, theNFLsaid officials had been in contact with Eagles medical personnel and the Cleveland Clinic in London throughout Hurts’ treatment.“The league’s chief medical officer, Dr Allen Sills, arranges for medical resources with leading providers in every international market with approval from the NFL Players Association,” the league said. “Medical care for players is provided by club medical staff in coordination with independent doctors.”Sills and other officials were expected to address reporters at the league’s annual fall meeting later Tuesday in New York.Hurts is on injured reserve and expected to miss the rest of the season after a blood clot in his left calf traveled to his lungs. The Eagles and his agent, Nicole Lynn, said Monday that Hurts has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli.His treatment involves blood thinners, and Hurts will not be allowed to participate in any football activities until he is no longer taking them.Hurts played against Jacksonville in London on 11 October, three days after informing medical staff of the injury following practice. He was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a superficial vein thrombosis in his left calf.Explore more on these topicsPhiladelphia EaglesNFLUS sportsShareReuse this content

title: Brock Purdy becomes highest-rated passer in NFL history as 49ers stay perfect | NFL | The Guardian
description: Brock Purdy threw a touchdown pass, Christian McCaffrey ran for two scores and the San Francisco 49ers held on to beat the Washington Commanders
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Brock Purdy threw a touchdown pass, Christian McCaffrey ran for two scores and the San Francisco 49ers held on to beat the Washington Commanders
Content: Brock Purdy and the 49ers are top of the NFC West.Photograph: Jed Jacobsohn/APView image in fullscreenBrock Purdy and the 49ers are top of the NFC West.Photograph: Jed Jacobsohn/APNFLBrock Purdy becomes highest-rated passer in NFL history as 49ers stay perfectWashington Commanders 17–23 San Francisco 49ersNiners move to 6-0 but are pushed hard by WashingtonAssociated PressMon 19 Oct 2026 23.42 EDTLast modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 07.24 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBrock Purdy threw a touchdown pass, Christian McCaffrey ran for two scores and the San Francisco 49ers held on to beat theWashington Commanders23-17 on Monday night for their sixth straight win to open the season.The Niners followed up an emotional win last week at division rival Seattle by building a 20-point lead and holding off the Commanders (1-4-1) with two late defensive stops.The Rams have managed to transform themselves from a superteam to a midteamRead more“[The defense] did it for us all game, I’m proud of those guys ... our defense balled,” Purdy said after the game.Jayden Daniels threw two touchdown passes in the second half to cut that 20-point deficit to 23-17, but Malik Mustapha broke up a fourth-down pass to Treylon Burks near the goalline with 1:54 to play to preserve the lead.Washington got the ball back at its 46 with 52 seconds remaining and moved down to the 28 before Daniels was called for intentional grounding, giving the Commanders one last play from the 40. Daniels was then sacked by Keion White and Ogbo Okoronkwo before he could throw up a desperation pass.The Niners extended their best start of a season since winning their first eight games in 2019 on the way to a Super Bowl appearance.Purdy started the game fast with a 24-yard strike to Mike Evans, who later left the game with an achilles injury, on the third play of the game and an 11-yard touchdown to George Kittle to finish that drive. Purdy went 21 for 29 for 264 yards and officially becamethe highest-rated quarterback in NFL historyas he passed the 1,500-attempt threshold to qualify. His 105.6 rating is ahead of Lamar Jackson’s 102.7.The Commanders were unable to bounce back from last week’s tie against the New York Giants, when they mismanaged the clock in overtime to cost them a chance at a game-winning field goal.The game was one-sided early with the 49ers scoring touchdowns on the first two drives on Purdy’s pass to Kittle and a one-yard run by McCaffrey.San Francisco expanded the lead to 20-3 late in the half on McCaffrey’s second touchdown run as the Niners gained as many first downs (17) in the first half as the Commanders ran plays.The Commanders lost star receiver Terry McLaurin to what looked like a severe knee injury during the game, and he is likely to miss a significant amount of time.“He’s a brother to me. It sucks,” Daniels said. “You see how hard he works ... Praying for Terry. He’s been there for me through a lot since I came into this league, the adverse times I went through last year and so far this year, and he’s been right by my side. I love Terry and appreciate him a lot.”Explore more on these topicsNFLWashington CommandersSan Francisco 49ersUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: US under-17 women beat Samoa 17-0 for biggest win in World Cup history | USA women's football team | The Guardian
description: Maddie DiMaria became the first player since Erling Haaland to score six goals at any age-level World Cup as the Americans opened the tournament with a rout
Author: Ella Brockway
Headline: Maddie DiMaria became the first player since Erling Haaland to score six goals at any age-level World Cup as the Americans opened the tournament with a rout
Content: Carolina Reyna became the third of her family to paly in a Fifa World Cup, scoring in the process.Photograph: Judit Cartiel/FIFA/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenCarolina Reyna became the third of her family to paly in a Fifa World Cup, scoring in the process.Photograph: Judit Cartiel/FIFA/Getty ImagesUSA women's football teamUS under-17 women beat Samoa 17-0 for biggest win in World Cup historyResult is largest margin at any age level of a World CupDiMaria is first to score six at Fifa finals since HaalandTournament is in year two of expanded 24-team fieldElla BrockwayTue 20 Oct 2026 11.15 EDTLast modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 12.35 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe United States began their U-17 Women’s World Cup campaign on Monday with a record-setting 17-0 win over Samoa the biggest win at any age level in World Cup history.The result surpassed the previous record for margin at an 11-a-side World Cup, a 16-0 win by Morocco against New Caledonia in the 2025 U-17 men’s World Cup. Ten players scored for the US, and forward Maddie DiMaria led with six goals in Salé, Morocco.“I wasn’t aware [we were breaking a record], but I’m super proud of this group and it’s nice that they have something like that behind their name,” US coach Ciara Crinion told Fifa’s website.DiMaria, a 17-year-old high-schooler from St Louis who is committed to play in college at North Carolina, scored her first goal 63 minutes into the match. It was the most goals by a US player ever in any match and the most by any player in a Women’s World Cup match at any level.She is the first player to net six goals in a single match at a Fifa finals since Erling Haaland scored nine at the U-20 men’s World Cup in 2019.“That means everything; he’s an inspiration,” DiMaria said of Haaland. “To be the next player behind that is just such an honor. I’m super blessed to have all those girls finding me in the right places.”The US led 9-0 by half-time on Monday and finished the match with 58 shots. Carolina Reyna, the younger sister of USMNT midfielder Gio Reyna, and 15-year-old Loradana Paletta each scored twice. Samoa goalkeeper Susahna Peacock made 13 saves.Samoa appeared in their first U-17 Women’s World Cup last year. Fifa expanded the field from 16 to 24 teams beginning in 2025 and is staging both the men’s and women’s U-17 World Cups annually through 2029 in an effort to prioritize youth development. Samoa are one of seven teams to make their U-17 Women’s World Cup debuts in the past two years, and expanded fields with countries at varying levels of development can make for lopsided score lines.The result brought back memories of the 13-0 win by the senior US team over Thailand at the 2019 Women’s World Cup in France. Alex Morgan scored five goals for the US in that game, after which criticsaccusedthe Americans of running up the score. The 2019 tournament was the first played with an expanded field of 24 teams.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“The way we respect our opponent is we don’t take it lightly,” US midfielder Julie Ertzsaid after that 2019 match. “We take any opponent we have very seriously. We prepare the same way. We have our scouting reports. We train with intensity. And that’s how we show we’re not going to take any opponent lightly.”The US play their next group-stage game Thursday against Kenya, who lost their opener 3-0 to China. The Americans have never won the tournament; they reached the final in the inaugural editions in 2008 and have only reached one semi-finals since, in 2024. North Korea are the reigning champions.Explore more on these topicsUSA women's football teamUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: World Series will have first-time champion as Rays set up showdown with Brewers | MLB | The Guardian
description: Freddy Peralta threw 5.1 gritty innings, Junior Caminero and Yandy Díaz each hit a two-run homer and the Tampa Bay Rays beat the Cleveland Guardian
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Freddy Peralta threw 5.1 gritty innings, Junior Caminero and Yandy Díaz each hit a two-run homer and the Tampa Bay Rays beat the Cleveland Guardian
Content: The Rays celebrate after returning to the World Series for the first time since 2020.Photograph: Mike Stobe/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenThe Rays celebrate after returning to the World Series for the first time since 2020.Photograph: Mike Stobe/Getty ImagesMLBWorld Series will have first-time champion as Rays set up showdown with BrewersTampa Bay beat Guardians to seal ALCS in six games7-3 Game 6 win set up by strong Freddy Peralta startAgenciesMon 19 Oct 2026 23.13 EDTLast modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 00.50 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFreddy Peralta threw 5.1 gritty innings, Junior Caminero and Yandy Díaz each hit a two-run homer and the Tampa Bay Rays beat theCleveland Guardians7-3 in Game 6 of the American League Championship Series on Monday night to advance to the World Series for the third time in the franchise’s 29 seasons.The Rays will face theMilwaukee Brewerswho, like Tampa Bay, are seeking to win their first-ever World Series. A sellout crowd of 40,230 fans waved yellow-and-blue rally towels, rang cowbells and chanted “Let’s go Rays!” throughout the night at Tropicana Field, which needed major renovations after Hurricane Milton shredded the roof two years ago and caused extensive damage throughout the stadium.“This is for you!” Caminero yelled to the crowd after Monday’s game. “Let’s go! I can’t hear you!”The Rays played their 2025 home games across the bay in Tampa at the New York Yankees’ spring training complex, got new ownership before this season and secured a new stadium deal to be ready in 2029 near the NFL’s Buccaneers. They returned to the Trop to win 55 games in the regular season. Only Milwaukee had that many home wins this year.The loss extended Cleveland’sWorld Serieschampionship drought to 78 years. Cleveland led the AL with 41 comeback victories this season, but fatigue clearly caught up with the Guardians as Tampa Bay closed out the series. The Guardians didn’t hold a lead over the final 25 innings.“I couldn’t be more proud of our group,” Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said. “It just hurts. It stings. Really felt like we had a team to go and just weren’t able to get there.”Hall of Famers v bunch of gamers: the Dodgers’ exit proves money can’t buy everythingRead moreThe best-of-seven World Series between low-payroll pennant winners opens Friday night in Milwaukee. It will be the first World Series between title-less teams since the Philadelphia Phillies defeated the Kansas City Royals in 1980. Just five of the currentMLB30 teams have never won a title, with Colorado, San Diego and Seattle also ringless.“The city is ready. I know that the fans are ready, and I know that we’ll be ready,” said Milwaukee’s Jake Bauers, MVP of the four-game sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NL Championship Series.Milwaukee’s Jacob Misiorowski heads the pitchers with his 100 mph-plus heat, and each team features a dynamic 22-year-old anchoring the lineup: Jackson Chourio of the Brewers and Junior Caminero of the Rays. Tampa Bay’s Peralta and Drew Rasmussen could pitch against their former teams.The Brewers started as the expansion Seattle Pilots in 1969, then were bought by Bud Selig’s group in bankruptcy court and moved to Milwaukee for the 1970 season. The team’s only Series trip was a seven-game loss to St Louis in the 1982 Suds Series, back when the Brewers were in the American League.Tampa Bay launched as the expansion Devil Rays in 1998 and dropped the “Devil” ahead of the 2008 season. The team’s two World Series appearances ended with losses to Philadelphia in 2008 and the Dodgers in the pandemic-shortened 2020 season.Milwaukee had MLB’s 19th-highest payroll as of 31 August. Tampa Bay were 25th. Not since 1991 had both pennant winners been among the bottom 50% in player spending. Minnesota were 15th among 26 teams when they beat Atlanta (19th) in seven games.Explore more on these topicsMLBWorld SeriesTampa Bay RaysMilwaukee BrewersCleveland GuardiansBaseballUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Angel Reese’s superb 30-point double-double helps Dream even WNBA finals | WNBA | The Guardian
description: Angel Reese scored a game-high 30 points as the Atlanta Dream defeated the Golden State Valkyries 79-65 to level their best-of-seven WNBA finals series
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Angel Reese scored a game-high 30 points as the Atlanta Dream defeated the Golden State Valkyries 79-65 to level their best-of-seven WNBA finals series
Content: Angel Reese celebrates victory in Game 2 of the WNBA finals.Photograph: Ezra Shaw/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenAngel Reese celebrates victory in Game 2 of the WNBA finals.Photograph: Ezra Shaw/Getty ImagesWNBAAngel Reese’s superb 30-point double-double helps Dream even WNBA finalsAtlanta’s 79-65 victory levels series at 1-1Reese scores 30 points and grabs 16 reboundsValkyries outplayed in second-half of defeatAgenciesMon 19 Oct 2026 22.44 EDTLast modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 00.49 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAngel Reese sent the message loud and clear to her teammates: “I need the ball! I need the ball!”In front of the Golden State Valkyries’ raucous home crowd, the Atlanta star had no choice but to raise her voice – and Reese knew she had to raise her game, too.‘I’m supposed to be here’: Angel Reese’s road from ridicule to the WNBA finalsRead moreShe delivered with 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2 of theWNBAfinals after struggling down the stretch in the series opener, and the Dream stymied Golden State on both ends in the second half to beat the Valkyries 79-65 on Monday night and even the best-of-seven series at one game apiece.“For me, I think I let my team down last game not really contributing as much as I could in the second half,” Reese said. “Not even just about scoring, my screen quality, me hustling and running to get rebounds, just doing the things that they know me to do. So I just wanted to make sure I came out tonight and left my mark and did whatever I could to get the win, and I think I did that tonight.”Quick GuideWNBA finals 2026ShowScheduleBest-of-seven series. All times Eastern.Sat 17 OctGame 1:Golden State 68, Atlanta 64Mon 19 OctGame 2:Atlanta 79, Golden State 65Wed 21 OctGame 3: Golden State at Atlanta, 8pm (USA/CNBC)Sat 24 OctGame 4: Golden State at Atlanta, 1pm (NBC)Mon 26 OctGame 5: Atlanta at Golden State, 8pm (USA/CNBC)Thu 29 OctGame 6: Golden State at Atlanta, 8pm* (USA/CNBC)Sat 31 OctGame 7: Atlanta at Golden State, 8pm* (USA/CNBC)*-if necessaryHow to watchIn the US, the series will air on NBC, USA Network and CNBC, with all games streaming on Peacock. In the UK, it will be carried by Sky Sports. In Australia, fans can watch through WNBA League Pass, with selected coverage also available through ESPN.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Rhyne Howard set a WNBA finals record with six steals, Allisha Gray added 18 points, and Jordin Canada contributed 13 points, 10 assists and seven rebounds as the Dream earned the franchise’s first finals victory after going winless in three previous trips – 0-10 overall. They now head home having salvaged a split in front of the boisterous “Ballhalla” crowd at Chase Center.“It’s just the next step of who Atlanta is,” Reese said.Reese became the third player with at least 30 points and 15 rebounds in a WNBA finals game, joining Jonquel Jones for Connecticut in 2019 and Breanna Stewart for Seattle in 2020.Atlanta coach Karl Smesko could see the focus in his superstar’s face before the game, and Reese’s teammates also saw it.“She was definitely way more aggressive, she had a great game,” Valkyries center Kiah Stokes said. “We let everyone kind of have their way.”Game 3 is Wednesday in Atlanta, where the next two games have been moved to the NBA’s Hawks’ State Farm Arena so more fans can attend. It holds more than 17,000, compared with the Dream’s regular home, Gateway Center Arena, which accommodates only 3,500.Chase Center holds 18,064 and has sold out every game since the Valkyries began playing last year.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly for the 2026 WNBA seasonSign up toWNBA 30A limited run women’s basketball newsletter dedicated to the league’s historic 30th season.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionGabby Williams finished with 14 points on 3-for-15 shooting after she was the only Golden State player to score in double figures with 26 pointsin Saturday’s 68-64 Game 1 win. The Valkyries shot 34.4% and went 7 for 24 from three-point range.“We shot terribly,” point guard Veronica Burton said. “We missed shots that we make all the time.”Foul trouble almost did in the Dream this time – but Reese simply wouldn’t have it. She went scoreless in the second half of the opener but delivered the big baskets and key defensive stops two days later, finishing 10 for 16 from the floor while dishing out three assists and blocking two shots.“We watched film and saw the things that we messed up on. When I said that they didn’t do anything to mess us up, it was literally just us,” Reese said. “And we can see that tonight. And we’re gonna carry that over in Atlanta. Atlanta, y’all better pull up and pop out, I’m looking forward to it.”Atlanta scored 24 points off Golden State’s 19 turnovers to hand the Valkyries their first loss in regulation since a 73-70 defeat at Chicago on 21 August. The Dream had scored just eight points off turnovers in Game 1 but returned to the defensive formula that had carried Atlanta this far.“We just got back to our identity about who we are and kept our foot on the pedal,” Reese said. “We didn’t let up and everybody was just on the same page, we had each other’s back. That’s just Atlanta basketball.”Explore more on these topicsWNBAAtlanta DreamGolden State ValkyriesBasketballnewsShareReuse this content

title: Arsenal’s David Raya hits back at ‘boring’ label as Arteta defends side’s style of play | Bayern Munich | The Guardian
description: David Raya says he does not care if rival supporters call Arsenal ‘boring’ as they prepare to face Bayern Munich in the Champions League
Author: David Hytner
Headline: David Raya says he does not care if rival supporters call Arsenal ‘boring’ as they prepare to face Bayern Munich in the Champions League
Content: David Raya is not interested in what people think about Arsenal’s style of play.Photograph: MI News/NurPhoto/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenDavid Raya is not interested in what people think about Arsenal’s style of play.Photograph: MI News/NurPhoto/ShutterstockBayern MunichArsenal’s David Raya hits back at ‘boring’ label as Arteta defends side’s style of playGoalkeeper brushes off criticism before Bayern clashKompany could miss game with virus affecting his legsDavid Hytnerin MunichTue 20 Oct 2026 16.00 EDTFirst published on Tue 20 Oct 2026 11.37 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleDavid Raya says he does not care if rival supporters call Arsenal “boring” as his manager,Mikel Arteta, insisted that critics of the team’s style were only a “very small minority”.Arsenal made it 10 wins out of 11 in all competitions for the season whenthey beat Nottingham Forest1-0 at the City Ground on Sunday. But it was a day when Noni Madueke’s late goal papered over a flat and one-paced performance. Arteta admitted his players had to be better in attacking terms and the discussion over how they are able to get the job done has tracked them to Germany where they face Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Wednesday night.Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan WilsonRead moreRaya sought to cut through the external noise when he was asked whether the criticism irritated him and his teammates. “No it doesn’t,” the goalkeeper said. “People have their own opinions. We have our own opinion. At the end of the day, we have lost one game in 11 this season and if you call that boring or irritating … I don’t know what to say. We enjoy playing football. We enjoy going out there every single day to win football matches and that’s the most important thing.”Arteta is focused on the glamour tie against Bayern, who will be without the suspended Michael Olise and might not have their manager,Vincent Kompany, in the dugout. He has been laid low by a viral infection that has also affected his legs. Arteta’s attitude to those who throw stones in Arsenal’s direction is that there will always be gripes about every club.“If you analyse all the top teams in England and I go: ‘OK, what are they talking about?’ They all have a list [of things about them],” he said. “None of us are perfect and thank God that we are not perfect and we can still improve, even though we have won the amount of games we have done because otherwise the next day, what do you do? You just expect to be better than the opponent and that’s it. Especially in the Premier League, we know that is very far from the reality.”Arteta sought to introduce a note of levity. “I don’t have that impression [about there being a debate over Arsenal’s style] because I heard it was incredible,” he said. “Because we scored so many goals, we have more possession, more shots, different players participating, no goals from set pieces … so the story is completely different to last year. I think we are talking about a very small minority and the other ones they know they have enjoyed a lot the way we have played and dominated games this year. We have proven that, so that’s my opinion.”Arteta knows that Bayern will bring the game to Arsenal; perhaps it will be a relief not to face low-block opponents and it might allow his team to be more expansive.“We know the kind of game that we’re going to play,” he said. “Both teams are very clear on that and we experienced that at the Emirates [last season, when Arsenal won 3-1]. It’s going to be a very similar one in many moments. A low block demands a different kind of game to a high block, to a team that is constantly putting the ball in the last line. But still on Sunday, I think we could have done things better and that’s in our hands. We need to recognise that openly, as well.”Arteta is never short of intensity or motivation and he went back tolast season’s Champions League finaldefeat by Paris Saint-Germain on penalties to illustrate how wildly the fire burns inside of him.“I tried [to get over it] but I haven’t managed to,” he said. “I tried for many weeks during the summer but when I see the ball, the scenes, I hear the music, I want it so badly. We know that we have to go step by step but I think that fire is within the team and all of us individually. We know what we had to go through – not being champions of Europe by a penalty. So, let’s try again.”View image in fullscreenVincent Kompany may not be in the dugout due to a viral infection.Photograph: Marcel Engelbrecht/firo sportphoto/Getty ImagesRaya remembered how Arsenal had only 28% of the ball against PSG but he feels they are better equipped to enjoy greater control against the elite. “I think so,” he said. “You have to see that in perspective, as well. It was our firstChampions Leaguefinal in so many years, we score in the fifth minute and you sit back a little bit knowing how good they are offensively. We didn’t want to give anything away. It is different now. You can see the way we play. You can see different type of ways of playing that we have. We are more prepared this year than last year.”Kompany is touch and go to make the game. He was unable to attend Bayern’s training session on Tuesday while he ceded the responsibility of the pre-match press conference to his assistant, Aaron Danks.Kompany had struggled through the6-1 home win over RB ­Leipzigin the Bundesliga on Saturday – after which the club’s sporting director, Max Eberl, addressed the media instead of him. There have been reports in Germany that Kompany needed to lie down on his sofa at home after the Leipzig game and that the infection had affected an existing hip problem which meant he could hardly walk.“It has affected his legs at times,” Danks said. “He’s felt some pain in his legs. I’m not sure about the reports about him lying down on the couch. I think we can all have a lie down on the couch after a game. It’s just a virus. The doctors and experts know way more than I do. The most important thing we have encouraged is that he rests; he takes the time he needs – however long that may be.“Unfortunately, I can’t give you any more – whether that’s tomorrow or whether that’s two or three days’ time. I don’t know.We just take it day by day and see how he is. Getting Vince to rest is a challenge. You know him as a person. He’s a real leader. He works hard.”Danks will take charge of the team against Arsenal if Kompany cannot make it, just as he did last season during the epic Champions League semi-final, first leg against PSG when Kompany was suspended. PSG won 5-4 at the Parc des Princes that night before progressing 6-5 on aggregate.Birmingham-born Danks, who briefly took caretaker charge of Aston Villa in 2022 and has coached at various clubs including Anderlecht and Middlesbrough, said he would be in communication with Kompany “in some shape or form” if the manager was not able to come to the stadium.Explore more on these topicsBayern MunichArsenalChampions LeagueMikel ArtetaVincent KompanynewsShareReuse this content

title: Doué and Vitinha burn bright as brittle Barcelona come unstuck against PSG | Champions League | The Guardian
description: Amid an ongoing state of civil unrest, Paris turned its attention to football as Vitinha’s late strike helped PSG to a 4-2 win against Barcelona
Author: Barney Ronay
Headline: Amid an ongoing state of civil unrest, Paris turned its attention to football as Vitinha’s late strike helped PSG to a 4-2 win against Barcelona
Content: Vitinha celebrates after putting PSG back in front late on.Photograph: Matthieu Mirville/ZUMA Press Wire/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenVitinha celebrates after putting PSG back in front late on.Photograph: Matthieu Mirville/ZUMA Press Wire/ShutterstockChampions LeagueDoué and Vitinha burn bright as brittle Barcelona come unstuck against PSGBarney Ronayat Parc des PrincesTue 20 Oct 2026 17.08 EDTLast modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 18.49 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFire, noise, fury, a sense of empty energy. And across town, a football match too. Do any of these randomly pitched autumnal Champions League fixtures mean anything? Probably not when you’reParis Saint-Germainand Barcelona, and the only game in town is risk-free TV income and a semi-guaranteed place in the knockout stuff.But this was still a dazzling occasion at the Parc des Princes, where the champions of France and Spain played out a light, open, frictionless, exhibition-style game of football. PSG finished 4-2 winners, having been pegged back to 2-2 midway through the second half. But this was also a game where the score almost did not seem to matter, and where the only really hard message was the frailty of theBarcelonabackline and PSG’s thrilling attacking energy in these midweek A-games.Foden hat-trick helps Manchester City cut through noise and crush AEK AthensRead more“Debris! Debris! DEBRIS!” the insanely loud PA announcer screamed into his mic before kick-off, in what appeared to be a poor-taste tribute to the current state of the nation’s capital, although it may also have been “du bruit”.In the hours leading up to this game France’s interior minister had specifically ruled out postponing the whole thing due to the ongoing state of civil unrest, the kind of statement that is no doubt intended to sound reassuring, but which also generates its own kind of whiplash.Paris is burning. Paris is always burning. No, but Parisreally is burning this time. The main site of the violence of the last few days is three miles east of the Parc, which lurks by the ring road in one of Paris’s slightlynégligéinner quarters, rising up like a vast concrete alien doughnut in between the townhouses.On matchday it required a degree of cognitive dissonance to take in these two opposing spectacles. On one hand the piles of charred bikes and the mass looting which has, in reassuringly Parisian style, seemed to focus on elite high-fashion brands. Chanel will rue the day.In the middle of which Paris also hosted this glittering treat of a football match, stuffed with so many throwaway little delicacies, like an elite artisan patisserie. Before kick-off there were leaping tongues of flame, a laser show spectacular, and a vast tifo at one end showing a ghoulish PSG serial killer type attacking the Barcelona badge with his blood-soaked chainsaw. The message here seemed to be: we are confident. We believe in our process. And we will hack you to death.View image in fullscreenDésiré Doué strikes to give PSG the lead in the first half.Photograph: Julien de Rosa/AFP/Getty ImagesFrom the start this was a high-grade, disarmingly open game. For Hansi Flick’s Barcelona it represented a genuine test of method. Here we have an elite team that plays with a studied disregard for some of the tenets of positional defensive play. We will press forward and trust what lies behind. We will also give up on the basic idea of marking pretty much from the kick-off, as it turned out.With one minute gone PSG should have scored. A quick diagonal passing move from right to left put Khvicha Kvaratskhelia in space. His shot pinged off a post and back to an offside Ousmane Dembélé, who shinned wide of an open goal.There was a fury to PSG in those opening minutes, the front players finding angles and free channels. Pedri and Marc Bernal in central midfield took a while to settle for Barça. Bernal is pure La Masia, a baby-faced 19-year-old Catalan, misleadingly so, as he also has the physique of a rugby union flanker. And Pedri is of course the kind of footballer who glides through these occasions, so casual you half expect to look down and notice he’s playing in flip-flops and holding a Calippo.Before long Barcelona were making chances of their own, Dani Olmo setting off on a couple of surging deep runs, Anthony Gordon almost getting on the end of a cutback.João Cancelo was booked with 16 minutes gone for a lunge on Désiré Doué, a disastrous state of affairs for any full-back faced with this nightmare of feints and fast-twitch feet. And two minutes later Dembélé was off, injured chasing the ball, replaced by Ferran Torres. Maybe he should play a bit more, get match fit.View image in fullscreenXavi Espart scores his first Champions League goal to equalise for Barcelona at 1-1.Photograph: David Ramos/Uefa/Getty ImagesStill the game just zinged from end to end. Raphinha had a close-range shot blocked by Matvey Safonov after a nice pass from Gordon. PSG had three shots blocked or saved in the space of six seconds on 28 minutes, Joan García saving brilliantly low down.And on 38 minutes PSG deservedly took the lead. The goal was in keeping with the game, expertly hi-tech but also strangely easy and open. Lamine Yamal essayed an ambitious chipped clearance. João Neves took the ball back. It fell to Doué, and he had time to jink inside, feel the space around him, and shoot low inside the post.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionPSG were bossing this by now, Kvaratskhelia running up and down the gears on the left, such a beautifully inventive presence, socks crumpled down around his ankles, all mooching straggly menace, as though the base player from Shed Seven has reinvented himself as a state of the art elite European inside forward.By the break Barcelona were hanging on, overrun in midfield. And the second half was more of the same: mobile, relentless, high-grade product, lovely attacking interchanges, occasional large spaces in the Barcelona backline.Doué forced another fine close-range save, played in by Vitinha. On 55 minutes Barcelona equalised, Xavi Espart galloping through the left side of the PSG defence and smashing a shot into the net off the hands of Safonov. The PA announcer gave the goal to Lamine Yamal, because, well, great branding. But it was Espart’s first in Europe, the second of his career. He’s 19, hyper-versatile, another dreamy Catalan youth-teamer.Barça brought on Rodri, absent from the starting XI, Flick admitted afterwards, solely with the weekend’sclásicoin mind. For a while order was restored, Rodri strolling around like the only grownup on the pitch.View image in fullscreenVitinha fires in from the edge of the box as PSG retake the lead late on.Photograph: Dave Winter/ShutterstockBut PSG always have tools to hurt you. Doué sliced open the right side again and crossed for Fabián Ruiz to hit the post from six yards out. From the corner Lucas Hernandez had the space to leap and produce a wonderful finish, thumped off the meaty part of the forehead high into the top corner.Seven minutes later it was 2-2. This was a strange goal, scored by Lamine Yamal after a wonderful run in from the right and a lofted near-post finish that in the moment either looked like a mistake from Safonov or a moment of pure invention.Two minutes after that it was 3-2 to PSG as the game kept on running to its own speed, this time a controlled first-time shot from Vitinha, seizing on a bouncing ball near the edge of the box. Ruiz added a fourth four minutes from the end.The game against Lyon at the weekend will mitigate against the usual round of rotations, and injuries did begin to bite a little here. But PSG still finished like a machine built for these occasions, operating always with strength in reserve, and quite clearly the most potent midweek team in Europe once again.Explore more on these topicsChampions LeagueParis Saint-GermainBarcelonaEuropean club footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Football regulator has ‘absolute power’ to force Manchester City sale if verdict upheld | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: The Independent Football Regulator’s chair, David Kogan, has said the watchdog has powers to make Manchester City’s owners sell the club
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The Independent Football Regulator’s chair, David Kogan, has said the watchdog has powers to make Manchester City’s owners sell the club
Content: David Kogan, chair of the Independent Football Regulator, is awaiting the outcome of Manchester City’s appeal before commenting on a potential further investigation.Photograph: Jon Super/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenDavid Kogan, chair of the Independent Football Regulator, is awaiting the outcome of Manchester City’s appeal before commenting on a potential further investigation.Photograph: Jon Super/ShutterstockManchester CityFootball regulator has ‘absolute power’ to force Manchester City sale if verdict upheldIFR chair David Kogan insists regulator has power to actCity have appealed against Premier League’s chargesPress AssociationTue 20 Oct 2026 19.34 EDTLast modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 20.23 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Independent Football Regulator (IFR) will have “absolute power” to force Manchester City’s owners to sell if they are ultimately found to have run the club improperly, the watchdog’s chair has said.Manchester City have beenfound guilty of circumventing Premier League rulesby an independent commission, which found they set up “sham” commercial arrangements to inflate revenues or reduce costs by over £900m over a nine-season period.David Squires on … Manchester City sailing into unknown Premier League watersRead moreThey were also found to have made “concerted efforts” to “stop and frustrate” the Premier League’s investigation into those arrangements. City have lodged an appeal, claiming the verdict “contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe”.David Kogan, the chair of the IFR, told podcastThe Rest Is Footballit was premature to talk about any action his organisation might take while the appeal was ongoing. Kogan did confirm, though, that the IFR had “absolute power” to force a sale by the club’s ownership, if that was felt to be appropriate.“We have the power to ask an owner to step away from a club if we believe that they run a club in a way that is neither fit, fair or done with propriety,” Kogan said. Asked if an owner could refuse to divest, Kogan replied: “No, no, no. We’ve got absolute power to do so.”On the possibility of the IFR investigating City, Kogan said: “I am not going to get pushed into making any judgement on this until we’ve seen all of those questions being answered. Then we will have to decide whether we’re going to mount our own investigation and come to a conclusion on that and what we’re going to do. And pre-empting that would be a colossal mistake.”Manchester City are majority-owned by Abu Dhabi United Group (Adug), an investment vehicle owned by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, a member of the Abu Dhabi royal family.Koganhas already pledged to resignif there is any political interference in any investigation the IFR may undertake into City, amid concerns it could create a diplomatic issue between the United Kingdom and the United Arab Emirates.Kogan’s comments came amid fresh scrutiny of Manchester City’s finances by the UK’s accounting watchdog. In a letter to the House of Commons business, innovation, science and trade committee, the Financial Reporting Council (FRC) confirmed it assumed “regulatory consideration” of the matter on 30 September.The FRC said it was examining the independent commission’s findings and making “preliminary enquiries” to establish whether there were grounds for a formal investigation.Explore more on these topicsManchester CityPremier LeagueFootball politicsBusinessnewsShareReuse this content

title: Carrick insists Manchester United board back him after Ten Hag points to ‘toxic culture’ | Manchester United | The Guardian
description: Erik ten Hag has claimed Cristiano Ronaldo ‘let the team down’ during their time together at Manchester United
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: Erik ten Hag has claimed Cristiano Ronaldo ‘let the team down’ during their time together at Manchester United
Content: ‘I have a really good relationship with everybody at the club,’ said Michael Carrick. ‘We’ve got to win games of football.’Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAView image in fullscreen‘I have a really good relationship with everybody at the club,’ said Michael Carrick. ‘We’ve got to win games of football.’Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAManchester UnitedCarrick insists Manchester United board back him after Ten Hag points to ‘toxic culture’Manager acknowledges he needs to start winning gamesTen Hag accuses Cristiano Ronaldo of letting club downJamie Jacksonin ComoTue 20 Oct 2026 17.13 EDTFirst published on Tue 20 Oct 2026 06.43 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMichael Carrick believes Manchester United’s board continue to back him, although the manager admits he must start winning matches to keep his job. Carrick also denied there is a toxic culture at the club, after Erik ten Hag’s claim there had been when he was manager.Carrick’s side travel to Como on Wednesday for their third Champions League game, aiming for a third victory of the season in all competitions. Sunday’s 1-1 draw at Leeds left United 13th in the Premier League, having won only once.Cristiano Ronaldo receives 30-day suspension and £215 fine over Portugal walkoutRead moreTheir only other success was last month’s4-0 home win against Sabah, of Azerbaijan, in the Champions League. Carrick was asked on Tuesday if he feels backed by the executive.“Yeah – why wouldn’t I?” said the 45-year-old. “I’m in this position, I have a really good relationship with everybody at the club. We’ve got to win games of football and that’s what we’re striving to do.”Despite the poor results Carrick has not sought reassurance from the hierarchy. “Certainly not. I don’t need any reassurance,” he said. “It’s pretty clear. I know the role, my responsibilities. I know we’ve got to win ­football games for everything to flow and ­everything to fall into place.”Ten Hag was Carrick’s predecessor from April 2022 to October 2024. During his tenure the Dutchman claimed that the executive did not support him regarding some disciplinary ­matters. In early 2024 Jim ­Ratcliffe, who had recently become the largest ­single minority stakeholder, assumed control of the football department.View image in fullscreenErik ten Hag and Cristiano Ronaldo in 2022. ‘He let the team down, and he let me down,’ the former Manchester United manager said.Photograph: Ed Sykes/Action Images/Reuters“They are continuing the toxic culture, they fuel it, they give power to the players,” Ten Hag told the Athletic, referring to his time in charge.Ten Hag claimed thatCristiano Ronaldo“let the team down” ­when the Dutchman was managing United. The ­forward’s second spell at the club featured him walking out twice.“He let the team down and he let me down, because we planned with him,” said Ten Hag. He also questioned ­Ronaldo’s commitment, saying that after United were beaten 4-0 at Brentford in the second game of his tenure, the ­Portuguese refused to complete a run in training.“I confronted him with this,” Ten Hag said. “Many times I say: ‘Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can’t bring yourself in the box, you can’t score.”Carrick, who became interim manager in January and was appointed permanently in May, was asked if he has encountered toxicity at United. “No, I haven’t. The players, the staff, they’ve given us everything that they could give,” he said. “I couldn’t be happier with the togetherness.”Ten Hag led United to the FA Cup in 2024, but claimed the owners then failed to meet promises made during talks that led to him agreeing a contract extension.He said: “They promised me ­loyalty, they promised me backing, they promised communication, that we get aligned. We spoke about the issues. But the promises, they didn’t keep. “I said: ‘No selling Scott ­McTominay.’ And in the end they sold him. I got, of course, very embarrassed and disappointed.”Carrick was asked if Ten Hag’s comments about the leadership raised any red flags. In answering he mentioned Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and the chief executive, Omar Berrada.Raya does not care if Arsenal are deemed ‘boring’ as Arteta defends style of playRead more“Not for me, that’s Erik’s opinion, it’s totally wrong for me to comment or get involved, it’s nothing to do with me at that stage. We’re pretty stable. There’s certain conversations we have that we’re really clear with, with Jason with Omar, the owners, and to the players. It’s really important we’re all pulling in the same direction.”Carrick will be without nine players for Como: Leny Yoro is ­suspended and Ayden Heaven is ill, while Luke Shaw, Lisandro Martínez, Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford, Benjamin Sesko, Patrick Dorgu and Manuel Ugarte are injured.The absence of five frontline defenders (Yoro, Shaw, Heaven, Martínez and Dorgu) will force Carrick to field an unfamiliar backline that may include Matthijs de Ligt, who has not played since last November due to a back problem. An appearance for the 19-year-old left-back, Harry Amass, is also being considered.There is a severe weather warning for lightning and rain in Como on Wednesday that may affect the 5.45pm kick-off.Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitedErik ten HagCristiano RonaldonewsShareReuse this content

title: Champions League roundup: McTominay double leads Napoli past Bodø/Glimt | Champions League | The Guardian
description: Scott McTominay scored twice as Napoli edged Bodø/Glimt in a seven-goal thriller while 10-man Atlético Madrid drew with Stuttgart
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Scott McTominay scored twice as Napoli edged Bodø/Glimt in a seven-goal thriller while 10-man Atlético Madrid drew with Stuttgart
Content: Scott McTominay jumps for joy after Napoli retake the lead before half-time.Photograph: Alberto Pizzoli/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenScott McTominay jumps for joy after Napoli retake the lead before half-time.Photograph: Alberto Pizzoli/AFP/Getty ImagesChampions LeagueChampions League roundup: McTominay double leads Napoli past Bodø/GlimtMidfielder scores for first time since heart surgeryTen-man Atlético hang on for draw against StuttgartAssociated PressTue 20 Oct 2026 17.55 EDTLast modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 18.46 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleScott McTominay scored his first two goals of the season to helpNapolibeatBodø/Glimt4-3 and relieve pressure on the coach, Massimiliano Allegri. McTominay, who also hit a post, missed a month of the season after undergoing a surgical procedure in early September to treat an irregular heartbeat.Matteo Politano’s first-minute opener was cancelled out by Bodø’s Jens Petter Hauge. McTominay restored Napoli’s lead before the break only for Andreas Helmersen to again level for the Norwegian club.Doué and Vitinha burn bright as brittle Barcelona come unstuck against PSGRead moreThe Scotland midfielder struck again on 71 minutes and Odin Bjørtuft’s late own goal secured the result. Bodø still managed an injury-time consolation from Sondre Brunstad Fet.Atlético Madridheld on with 10 men for a 1-1 draw withStuttgart, foiling the German underdogs’ bid to join Paris Saint-Germain and Liverpool at the top of the table on nine points.Julián Alvarez’s goal for Atlético had cancelled out Jamie Leweling’s opener when the midfielder Morten Hjulmand made a reckless sliding tackle from behind on Angelo Stiller, resulting in a red card that left Atlético clinging on.Serhou Guirassy scored twice butBorussia Dortmundwasted plenty more chances in a 2-1 away win over Azerbaijan’sSabah.It wasn’t the sort of convincing victory the German team were hoping for, after last week’s loss to Bodø/Glimt and draw at Union Berlin which allowed Bayern Munich to take the top spot in the Bundesliga.View image in fullscreenSerhou Guirassy scores for Borussia Dortmund against Sabah.Photograph: Alexandre Simões/Borussia Dortmund/Getty ImagesPavel Kacor’s leaping volley in the 90th minute earnedSlavia Praguea 2-2 draw atFenerbahce, extending the hosts’ long wait for aChampions Leaguewin. The Turkish side had been leading 2-0 early on before a defensive blunder by Mattéo Guendouzi let the Czech team back into the game.PSVwon 1-0 againstPortothanks to Guus Til’s 57th-minute winner as the Portuguese side slumped to a third loss.Romacruised to a 4-0 win overSlovan Bratislavawith Mario Hermoso, Nahuel Molina and Niccolò Pisilli on the scoresheet before Donyell Malen added a fourth from the penalty spot.Explore more on these topicsChampions LeagueFenerbahceSlavia PragueSabahBorussia DortmundNapoliBodø/GlimtnewsShareReuse this content

title: Kulusevski and Maddison return to form but are Tottenham also back?  | Soccer | The Guardian
description: In today’s Football Daily: Spurs win a football match
Author: John Brewin
Headline: In today’s Football Daily: Spurs win a football match
Content: James Maddison (right) pops one into the top bin to give Tottenham the lead against Coventry.Photograph: Dylan Martinez/ReutersView image in fullscreenJames Maddison (right) pops one into the top bin to give Tottenham the lead against Coventry.Photograph: Dylan Martinez/ReutersFootball Daily newsletterSoccerKulusevski and Maddison return to form but are Tottenham also back?John BrewinTue 20 Oct 2026 10.39 EDTLast modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 11.12 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMAD FOR ITAs Tottenhamedged to victory over Coventry, a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? For it was he, playing 526 days since his last Spurs appearance. Much has changed though still much stays the same. Ben Davies’s deflected late clincher catapulted Spurs up to … 16th. When Kulusevski last played on 11 May 2025, Tottenham were 17th, the position in which they finished both that season and in 2025-26.So what has changed? Ange Postecoglou was tinned that summer despitewinning the Flamin’ Bigger Vase. Thomas Frank was an appointment the soccer sensibles agreed was smart. A coach with impeccable credentials in improving players, willing to work in tandem with club suits, an ideal apex for an org chart. With lovely hair, too.Frank was sent packingin February, his popularity ratings plunging to depths unseen since Alan Sugar had the bright idea of appointing George Graham, who had paid his gardener to shape his lawn into the Arsenal crest. In football’s world of irrelevant but interesting (you sure? – Football Daily Ed) coincidences, the last time Spurs beat Coventry in the league, when Sergiy Rebrov’s goalcompleted a 3-0 stroll in 2001, the manager’s programme notes had been written by Gorgeous George, who the day previously had been the recipient of Sugar’s “you’re fired” flex.Igor Tudor’s tenure resembled a slasher movie, an appointment on the nod from a sporting director, Fabio Paratici, who had already left. Classic Spurs. What could possibly go wrong? Everything, it turns out. Or close to, until Roberto De Zerbi was handed the keys and a control none of his predecessors commanded. The transfer spend has been heavy, and when Kulusevski arrived in the 87th minute on Monday, the game not yet won, he did so following an absence where Spurs signed 20 players either permanently or on loan, at a cost of £530m.Scoring Spurs’ opening goal on Monday was James Maddison. Football’s king of the oche was absent for almost as long Kulusevski.
