Last season, as De Zerbi attempted to arrest the slide towards relegation, ‘Madders’ initially sat on the bench on a vibes-only basis and closed out the season with not much more than 30 minutes of play, and had little time to do Maddison things like his arcing beauty against his hometown club on Monday, which opened the scoring for Spurs.Good feelings at last, following a sunshine break in Marbella where, according to De Zerbi, his players became less a squad than a family. “You have to play for your friend and your brother, not like 11 robot players on the pitch,”he cooed. With two of his stars back in tandem, De Zerbi’s enforcer intensity brought a first league win of the season, to help Tottenham off the bottom. “With them in the dressing room there is another atmosphere,” De Zerbi roared. Jam tomorrow? Glory, glory? Lads, it’s etc …LIVE ON BIG WEBSITEJoin Scott Murray from 8pm BST for Liverpool 2-1 Villarreal in the Bigger Cup action while Simon Burnton is on clockwatch action to bring you updates from PSG 3-3 Barcelona, Manchester City 4-1 AEK Athens, and more.QUOTE OF THE DAY“People still call me a ‘party boy’. That stigma has been overused and has followed me since I retired from football. I’m not saying I didn’t enjoy myself as a player. You never hear that I didn’t turn up for training or wasn’t fit … now I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time. I’m a manager” –Dwight Yorke speaks to Morgan Oforifrom his home in Dubai about his career ambitions, having been linked with the vacant Ghana job.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenDwight Yorke: ‘I’m straightforward. I don’t mess around, take shortcuts or do the job halfway.’Photograph: Christopher Pike/The GuardianFOOTBALL DAILY LETTERSdouble quotation markFurther to Peters and Lee [Monday’s Football Dailyletters] another 70s example that occurred to me was the West Ham players MervynDayand BillGreen. They were both in the West Ham United team from 1976-78, and in Carlisle United’s greatest season 1974-75. When Green was still at Carlisle, he played against West Ham’s Day. So plenty of Green Day commentary opportunities there. Of course, the band hadn’t formed yet, but who knows, perhaps they thought of the band’s name whilst watching some old 70s football footage” – Bob Dunning.double quotation markOn the subject of musical football matchups, all I can say is that it’s just a shame GarethBarrywas at Manchester City a few years too late to play alongside DavidWhite” – Tim Russell.double quotation markAs an aside to the music makers and fitba’, in the late 60s at the old Highbury, we would be entertained at every first team match by the local constabulary brass band. Such was the style of play, it did introduce a some element of entertainment into our visits to the old stadium” – Tommy Boyd (and, surprisingly, others).If you have any, please send letters tothe.boss@theguardian.com.Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day goes to … Bob Dunning. title: How Brazil’s election result could shape women’s football in the country | Women's football | The Guardian
description: Female players including Carlinha and Tayla Carolina have spoken out against the far right, who they fear will harm the women’s game as well as wider society
Author: Júlia Belas Trindade
Headline: Female players including Carlinha and Tayla Carolina have spoken out against the far right, who they fear will harm the women’s game as well as wider society
Content: Carlinha during a match between Sao Paulo and Corinthians earlier this month.Photograph: Foto Arena LTDA/Alamy Stock Photo/Alamy Live News.View image in fullscreenCarlinha during a match between Sao Paulo and Corinthians earlier this month.Photograph: Foto Arena LTDA/Alamy Stock Photo/Alamy Live News.Moving the Goalposts newsletterWomen's footballHow Brazil’s election result could shape women’s football in the countryFemale players including Carlinha and Tayla Carolina have spoken out against the far right, who they fear will harm the women’s game as well as wider societyJúlia Belas TrindadeTue 20 Oct 2026 08.28 EDTLast modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 13.20 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe day before the first round of Brazilian elections, the Estádio do Morumbi hosted the second leg of the Brazilian Women’s Championship final, in which São Paulo drew 1-1 with Corinthians to win 3-2 on aggregate and secure the Brasileirão Women’s title.It had been an incredible final but after the game the goalkeeper Carlinha used an interview to appeal to her fans: “Never again Bolsonaro in power,” she shouted to a record-breaking TV audience of 23 million people.Having lost her grandmother during the Covid-19 pandemic, Carlinha recalls the challenges faced by hundreds of thousands of Brazilian families when the far-right president Jair Bolsonarospread fake informationabout the virus while ignoring public appeals for the government to buy and distribute vaccinations. More than 700,000 Brazilians died during the pandemic. Now his son, Flávio, is standing against the 80-year-old incumbent leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.“I didn’t just think of [my grandmother] when I gave that interview, I think about her and miss her every single day,” Carlinha tells Moving the Goalposts. “I felt relieved after talking about my personal opinion in such an important moment of Brazilian democracy. I’m a journalism student and I know the impact if the right wins the elections.”Carlinha is one of several female football players who have used social media and their visibility to speak up before and during the presidential election, which will come to an end on Sunday with a second-round vote. The father of the Bolsonaro dynasty is currently under “humanitarian house arrest”, serving a 27-year sentence for a coup attempt.Carlinha’s club and international teammate, Tayla Carolina, went viral the weekend after discussing her family’s background and how public policies implemented during Lula’s government were important for her mother and grandmother, who have worked as cleaners throughout their lives and have since passed. “I’m from a very humble family, I’m a Black woman. I’ve studied in public schools and used the national healthcare system … my mum, dona Dora, worked for over a decade for someone who never paid her labour rights … and she worked until she couldn’t walk any more due to the cancer that took her from us. She never saw me play because she never had the time, she never rested,” she wrote. Her story resonates with many Brazilians who fought for shorter working weeks, approved earlier this week in congress.View image in fullscreenThe Brazil international Tayla Carolina has expressed her support for Lula’s policies.Photograph: Aude Alcover/Icon Sport/Getty ImagesTayla elaborates her point: “I’m from a country where most of the people are poor but the country is not seen as poor. It shows there are huge inequalities, which come from exploitation. Years have passed and there’s still a lot of inequality and I come from it … as a public figure, and someone who has lived similar lives to the majority of Brazilians, I feel the responsibility to speak up.”The player organisation Fifpro has just releaseda new studyshowing that nearly half of female football players think of early retirement owing to the psychological and financial pressures of the women’s game (800 professional players took part). With the Women’s World Cup being staged in Brazil next year both Carlinha and Tayla feel the election will have a huge impact on the game going forward.“There is one side that makes it quite clear how they feel about women’s rights,” says Carlinha, referring to, among other things, politicians such as Eduarda Campopiano, one of the most voted members of the São Paulo Assembly, who calls herself an “enemy of feminists” and has said she does not believe in femicide – that women and girls can be killed because they are women. Tayla also feels the need for policies to support the women’s game at a crucial moment. “We still need government incentives, so it may not be immediate, but the game will be affected, positively or negatively, depending on how the elections go.”Lula approved the World Cup law in June 2026, which regulates many aspects of the tournament, including how ministries, the Brazilian FA (CBF), state federations and clubs will commit to developing a legacy and supporting the women’s game in the country. The legacy plan, divided into four strands, proposes supporting access and permanence of girls and women in football, developing and professionalising the game, fighting gender- and racial-based discrimination, and enhancing the economic and cultural aspects of women’s football in Brazil. The commitment to the tournament is stated in Lula’s government plan. Bolsonaro’s proposals for women’s sport do not mention the World Cup; instead, he proposes “ensuring that women’s categories, from youth to elite, are played by athletes of the female sex, protecting women and tournaments from ideological agendas”.Brazilian football, men’s and women’s, has been heavily politicised for decades, and the rise of social media has led to an increase in players publicly supporting their political candidates. In the men’s game, the far right is often championed by the Santos and Brazil forward Neymar, who has showed support for the Bolsonaro family on many occasions. Tottenham’s Richarlison, meanwhile, is positioned on the left and this week accused Flávio Bolsonaro of “taking possession” of an island he says he bought a few years back.The country’s female players do not have the same number of followers on social media and cannot influence a big audience in the same way as the men. However, it is true that the result of the election is likely to have more of an impact on the women’s game than on the men’s.View image in fullscreenBrazilian students and activists march in downtown Rio de Janeiro to support Lula and protest against the far-right candidate, Flávio Bolsonaro.Photograph: Ellan Lustosa/ZUMA Press Wire/ShutterstockKely Nascimento, the daughter of late football legend Pelé and founder and executive director of the Nascimento Foundation, says: “Female players, female athletes, they don’t have the protection of wealth. What feeds the brilliance of Brazilian football are the players, and they mostly come from communities, favelas and other places that are going to be hugely affected by these elections. Women are more affected by all this, right?”Carlinha, who played in one of the two recent friendlies against Argentina, says playing for the national team at home is “one of the best feelings ever”. At both stadiums, in Porto Alegre and Recife, the crowd predominantly chanted in support of Lula, which could be heard over the TV commentary during the broadcast.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe politicisation of women’s football is not new, as Brazilian women’s football historian and author Aira Bonfim explains. “This is a hundred-year-old history, because we have episodes of women playing football in Brazil since 1915, and the women’s game reveals different perspectives of gender inequalities, racial inequalities, class, territory, which will affect the progress of the women’s game,” she says. “By knowing women’s football history, we can look at episodes which are equally as political, such as the ban on the women’s game [between 1941 and 1979], the persecution of women, and lies that were told so that female players would give up on it.”One of the pieces of history that she has uncovered in her research became a short film, which debuted earlier this month at the Rio Film Festival, The House of Dona Carlota, produced by Mymama Entertainment and directed by Lili Fialho and Bruna Linzmeyer, which tells the story of a woman who was arrested and persecuted because she led a women’s football team, Primavera Atlético Clube.It shows women’s football as a space of socialisation, sport and resistance to the Estado Novo dictatorship in the late 1930s and early 1940s. The women’s game was banned in Brazil for decades, and the World Cup in 2027 is where many hope its renewed development will be consolidated.“What’s at risk [in this election] is a waste of all of the human investments in building social legacy plans. There is also the risk of dismantling all political communication that has been done to support [the World Cup] through the ministries, cities and state governments. If you elect someone who did not make any commitments towards it, who did not commit to the World Cup or what it represents to women, it can be a huge loss,” Bonfim says. “Just the fact that during Jair Bolsonaro’s government he removed the status of the ministry of sports reveals how he feels about the sector.”The hosting of a Women’s World Cup is key in developing public policies and attracting investment and support. As Nascimento says: “There are girls all over Brazil for whom football is not just their dream, but it’s also how they get out of very awful situations. And there are amazing people doing God’s work all over Brazil just to get girls to play, to be educated in another way … for some reason, Brazil just makes football magic, and that’s not gender-specific. And there’s an enormous Brazil that is being ignored and taken advantage of.”There are many reasons for the international community to look closer at the second round of Brazil’s elections on Sunday, from how it can affect climate change, foreign policy and financial markets to many other issues. Women’s football, and all it represents, is one of them.Get in touchIf you have any questions or comments about any of our newsletters please emailmoving.goalposts@theguardian.com.This is an extract from our free email about women’s football, Moving the Goalposts. title: Animal rights group urges Crystal Palace to retire bald eagle mascot | Crystal Palace | The Guardian
description: Peta has urged Crystal Palace to retire their eagle mascot because, it says, the matchday experience can leave the bird ‘frightened, disoriented and panicked’
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: Peta has urged Crystal Palace to retire their eagle mascot because, it says, the matchday experience can leave the bird ‘frightened, disoriented and panicked’
Content: Phoenix the eagle is presented to Crystal Palace fans for first time in August 2024.Photograph: Sebastian Frej/MB Media/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenPhoenix the eagle is presented to Crystal Palace fans for first time in August 2024.Photograph: Sebastian Frej/MB Media/Getty ImagesCrystal PalaceAnimal rights group urges Crystal Palace to retire bald eagle mascotPeta calls on club to never again use a live animal mascot‘There’s no reason to drag a wild animal into a stadium’Ed AaronsTue 20 Oct 2026 08.00 EDTLast modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 13.33 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleA leading animal rights group has urgedCrystal Palaceto retire their American bald eagle mascot because, it says, the matchday experience can leave the bird “frightened, disoriented and panicked” and put spectators at risk.In a letter to Palace’s chief executive, Sharon Lacey, People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (Peta) called on the club to end Phoenix’s appearances at Selhurst Park and commit never to use a live animal mascot again.Crystal Palace to give Sage more time but manager under serious scrutinyRead morePalace, known as the Eagles since 1973 after the then manager Malcolm Allison changed their nickname from the Glaziers, introduced a pre-match display from Kayla the Eagle in 2010. She died in 2020 after a decade’s service but Kayla’s replacement, Phoenix, made her debut before the game against West Ham in August 2024 at four months old, meeting supporters in the fanzone and being introduced at half-time with her handler.Phoenix is based at the Eagle Heights Wildlife Foundation in Kent, and its website said at the time that she “had been carefully prepared for her prestigious role as Crystal Palace’s official live mascot since hatching”. Phoenix is not at every game but it is understood plans for her to make a maiden flight across the pitch before kick-off – a ritual Kayla for which was renowned – were abandoned at a match this season.In the letter seen by the Guardian, Peta said bright lights, loud noises and boisterous crowds mean stadiums are “no place for animals” and potentially put animals and spectators at risk. It detailed incidents of eagles that have collided with walls or glass windows and a falcon that landed on a spectator’s head, embedding its talons in the man’s scalp. Peta also referred to an incident involving Kayla in 2015 when a Charlton fan was found guilty of trying to punch her during a League Cup tie marred by crowd trouble.View image in fullscreenKayla the eagle, who died in 2020, in flight before a Crystal Palace game in 2014.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianDr Carys Bennett, Peta’s senior corporate projects manager, said: “Bald eagles are revered as symbols of freedom, yet Phoenix is being used as little more than a prop to entertain football fans. Crystal Palace already has a human mascot to energise supporters, so there’s no reason to drag a wild animal into a noisy, crowded stadium. Peta is urging the club to let Phoenix spread [her] wings and retire from matchday duties for good.”Palace did not respond to Peta’s letter or to a follow-up request last week. They have been contacted for comment. The Guardian sent a number of questions to Eagles Heights to ask about Phoenix’s welfare and did not receive a reply.Peta’s letter argued that eagles’ natural behaviours make the stadium environment unsuitable for them. In the wild, the birds can travel across vast territories and typically avoid close contact with humans. The organisation said even birds raised in captivity retain their natural instincts and may experience frustration and stress when unable to engage in natural behaviours.Benfica’s home matches feature appearances from a bald eagle called Águia Vitória – a custom that the Portuguese club started in 2003 when their new Estádio da Luz opened.Explore more on these topicsCrystal PalacePetanewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘I’m in a bad place’: Mark Allen says his snooker career may be over after defeat | Snooker | The Guardian
description: Mark Allen has said he ‘doesn’t see a future with snooker in it’ in an emotional interview after losing his first match since April’s Crucible semi-final defeat
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Mark Allen has said he ‘doesn’t see a future with snooker in it’ in an emotional interview after losing his first match since April’s Crucible semi-final defeat
Content: Mark Allen’s first-round loss in Belfast was his first appearance at a tournament since an agonising semi-final defeat at the Crucible in April.Photograph: George Wood/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMark Allen’s first-round loss in Belfast was his first appearance at a tournament since an agonising semi-final defeat at the Crucible in April.Photograph: George Wood/Getty ImagesSnooker‘I’m in a bad place’: Mark Allen says his snooker career may be over after defeatFormer world No 1 loses 4-2 to Jordan Brown in Belfast‘I don’t see a future with snooker in it,’ says tearful AllenPress AssociationTue 20 Oct 2026 14.54 EDTLast modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 17.42 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMark Allen said he was in a “bad place” and his snooker career could be over after losing to Jordan Brown in the first round of theNorthern IrelandOpen in Belfast.The 40-year-old was playing his first match since his world championship semi-final loss to Wu Yize in April. Allen missed a match-ball black off the spot at 16-15 in front and went on to lose the deciding frame to Wu, who went on to win the title.Allen has since stayed away from the tour due to personal issues that he has kept private – although they are understood not to relate directly to his Crucible defeat. After his 4-2 loss to Brown, a close friend who is also from Antrim, Allen indicated he is set to take another long break from the sport – and could make it permanent.Inan emotional interview with TNT Sportsafter the match, Allen said he was “really overwhelmed”, adding: “I’m in a bad place at the minute, so even just to go out there and try was tough.”“I think if I wasn’t playing Jordan I wouldn’t have come back,” the former world No 1 said. “I felt like if I was going to play one last time, playing here at the Waterfront, where it all started in 2005, against one of my best mates – I thought that was a better way to sign out.”Asked if he was serious about his threat to retire from professional snooker, Allen confirmed his view and continued: “I’ve been flooded with support but the problems are within. I just don’t see a future with snooker in it, if I’m honest.“It’s sad to say, because it’s all I’ve loved to do since I was 12 but the last few months has been really difficult and it’s put snooker into perspective for me. At the minute I’m just trying to survive.”Allow Instagram content?This article includes content provided byInstagram. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content,click 'Allow and continue'.Allow and continueIn a separate interview with BBC Sport NI, Allen said: “The last three months have been really, really difficult and I think even just being here today is an achievement. I am not going to announce [retirement] right now after a defeat, but it is something I have been contemplating for a while.”Allen, currently ranked No 12 in the world after his hiatus, has won 12 ranking tournaments in his career, including the 2022 UK Championship and two Northern Ireland Open titles. He has reached the world championship semi-finals three times, and lifted the Masters trophy in 2018.Brown, whose sole ranking title came at the 2021 Welsh Open, said: “First and foremost it’s just great to see Mark back playing. He obviously came through a tough time off the table and I’m with him every step of the way, like everybody is.“We’re all behind him. I miss him and I love him and we all just want to see him healthy and well and playing the game that he loves so much,” Brown added. “He’s a great player and a great guy.”Both the WorldSnookerTour and the sport’s governing body, the WPBSA, have provided support to Allen and have indicated their desire to continue helping him in any way they can.Allen is one of a number of high-profile players to exit this year’s Northern Ireland Open in the first round. Shaun Murphy was beaten 4-2 by Wales’ Liam Davies, with Mark Selby losing to Louis Heathcote by the same scoreline.The world No 1, Zhao Xintong, also lost 4-2 to Chinese compatriot Gao Yang while Neil Robertson went down 4-1 to Ricky Walden. Ronnie O’Sullivan also fell at the first hurdle, beaten 4-3 by Cheung Ka Wai of Hong Kong. The defending champion, Jack Lisowski, did advance to the last 32 with a 4-1 win over Huang Jiahao.Explore more on these topicsSnookerNorthern IrelandnewsShareReuse this content

title: England collapse to 87-run defeat by Pakistan in men’s tri-series cricket ODI – as it happened | Cricket | The Guardian
description: Pakistan’s young all-rounder Arafat Minhas starred with bat and ball as England were well beaten in Rawalpindi
Author: Tim de Lisle
Headline: Pakistan’s young all-rounder Arafat Minhas starred with bat and ball as England were well beaten in Rawalpindi
Content: 9h ago12.09 EDTTaha HashimMatch report: Pakistan win by 87 runsAfter the embarrassment of their English summer this was a welcome sight for Pakistan. A contest in front of their own, no Ollie Robinson to wobble down a lethal Dukes ball, and a format they are far more comfortable with. The result was an impressive victory against England, who fell 87 runs short in their first match of this one-day international tri-series.At the centre was Arafat Minhas, playing only his fifth ODI but already making a serious splash, finishing with astounding figures of six for 40. Oh, and he can bat too. The 21-year-old began with a half-century from No 7, resuscitating Pakistan’s innings alongside another newcomer, Hasan Nawaz, as 81 for four turned into a total of 302.Minhas’ left-arm spin was next, and he accounted for Harry Brook with a magical delivery as England crumbled, a decent position of 165 for three turning into 215 all out. Minhas was the closer, showing off another skill: he pulled off a direct hit to run out Gus Atkinson and end the game with 11.2 overs left.Arafat rips through England as Brook’s men wilt against Pakistan in tri-series openerRead moreShareUpdated at12.09 EDT

title: Jalen Hurts played through a blood clot. Are NFL players cattle? | Philadelphia Eagles | The Guardian
description: The Eagles quarterback’s recent health issues highlight how football’s toughness culture puts its players at risk
Author: Andre Gee
Headline: The Eagles quarterback’s recent health issues highlight how football’s toughness culture puts its players at risk
Content: Jalen Hurts is set to miss the rest of the NFL season.Photograph: Ali Habib/ZUMA Press Wire/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenJalen Hurts is set to miss the rest of the NFL season.Photograph: Ali Habib/ZUMA Press Wire/ShutterstockPhiladelphia EaglesJalen Hurts played through a blood clot. Are NFL players cattle?Andre GeeThe Eagles quarterback’s recent health issues highlight how football’s toughness culture puts its players at riskTue 20 Oct 2026 10.15 EDTLast modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 14.11 EDTShareJalen Hurts islikely to miss the rest of the NFL seasonafter an ultrasound revealed blood clots in his lungs. Thankfully, he’s now restricted from playing for the immediate future, meaning he won’t be risking serious complications – or even his life – as he did when he played in the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London.The quarterback complained to the Eagles’ medical staff of calf pain on 8 October,according to ESPN.The Eagles sayHurts flew to London with the rest of the team and, out of an “abundance of caution”, was given an ultrasound. The test found a superficial clot in his calf. Doing an ultrasound before the flight would’ve been the most prudent thing. The same for making him inactive after the clot was found. But instead, he played in the game on 11 October, as the medical staff and doctors in London agreed “that activity and mobility were important”. Hurts also practiced all last week before a follow-up ultrasound alsofound clots in his lungs.Brock Purdy becomes highest-rated passer in NFL history as 49ers stay perfectRead moreSome have celebrated Hurts’s performance against the Jaguarsas a feat of virility; to many it looks more like putting a player in real danger. His blood clots could have caused serious health issues during the flights or game. (One sports medicine doctortold NJ.com that Hurtswas “a walking risk”.) If his condition was dire enough that doctors reportedly told him in the early hours of Sunday morning not to sleep before the Jaguars game, he shouldn’t have been playing. Hurts’s agent, Nicole Lynn,clarified that he did get some sleepbefore facing the Jaguars, but the question remains: was the NFL’s London showcase so important that it was worth risking Hurts’s life?Asked about his decision to play Hurts,Eagles coach Nick Sirianni told reporters thathe relies on advice from medical staff. “I’m a football coach. I lean on our medical experts in every situation,” he said. “I have full trust and full faith in them. It’s not just me that has major care for our players. It’s them as well.”The Super Bowl LIX MVP is on blood thinners and hopefully on the road to healing, expected to make a full recovery. But his ordeal is the latest example of how football players are put in danger season after season.One piece of research from 2017found that a college player took hits to his head during a single game that were equivalent to multiple car crashes.A study published this yearfound that 215 of 235 brains of former NFL players donated for research showed signs of chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), a degenerative brain disease that can only be diagnosed after death. The NFL has said that it “continuously strives to make the game of football safer, including by implementing ⁠strategies to reduce concussions and head impacts” but players keep on suffering concussions, and others like Hurts find themselves in a football culture where playing through injury is commonplace.Last Wednesday, Hurtstold reportersthat his last week had been a “very unique experience” but declined to reveal the blood clot. No one has reported that he received any undue pressure from the Eagles or the league to play against the Jaguars. But it wouldn’t be shocking; this isn’t even the Eagles’ first controversial injury in London. In 2018, former Eagles tackleLane Johnson was reportedly “berated”by general manager Howie Roseman for saying he was unsure about playing because of a high ankle sprain. After suiting up, Roseman reportedly told him, “Good, you have your mouthpiece in, now you can’t say anything stupid.” Neither man has commented on the matter, but it appears to offer a glimpse of life in the good ol’ NFL, where admitting you’re impaired is stupidity. Johnson aggravated the ankle injury and suffered a knee injury during the game.Football culture demands players “tough it out” and get on the field. As former NFL receiver Bernard Berrianhas said, the tension “isn’t verbal” but is still “there” because, “as we say, you can’t make the team in the training room.” Former running back Clinton Portisechoed Berrianwhen he spoke about playing through 10 concussions in his career and rarely getting treatment: “You can’t make the club in the tub.” Portis said he was “really scared” of undergoing testing to assess his neurological health.You can see how the culture of the NFL makes players behave this way. With only61% of NFL contracts containing guarantees, andan average 56% year-to-year retention, the pressure to stay active and keep the checks coming in is rampant. Pretty much every job pressures its employees to perform in some capacity; only one entails 300lb men running full speed to tackle you for 17 games a season. Players shouldn’t be made to feel they need to be on the field, but the irrational “win now” pressure they face trickles down and paints them in two colors: as an asset or expendable. It’s inherently inhumane.The NFL has attempted to address injuries, and the threat of concussion and CTE in particular, but those efforts don’t seem to be enough. The league has changed kickoff rules and introducedoversized Guardian Capsto mitigate concussions, but football’s physical risks persist. A2018 studyin the Brain Neurology Journal revealed that subconcussive hits also contribute to CTE. And a 2025Wisconsin School of Medicine study concludedthat Guardian Caps did not reduce concussion rates in a sample of high school players. It’s unclear what seismic changes could actually address football’s inherent brutality. And the NFL’s struggles to stop it shows it is unsure – or doesn’t care enough – too.Hurts’s case also raises the specter of medical racism.Multiple studies have shownthat Black people and other minorities in the United States are less likely to receive adequate medical care than white people. It’s impossible to say whether the staff who treated Hurts looked at a strapping Black athlete and believed he could play a brutal game while suffering from blood clots. But the incident nonetheless conjureshistorical patterns and lived experiencesof Black peoplenot receiving proper care.Hopefully Hurts gets back on the field and has a long, healthy career. Regardless, the Eagles’ handling of his treatment should be a demarcation point for the league. From the top down, theNFLneeds to stop treating its labor force like cattle on a farm, as if their sole worth is in putting their bodies at risk.Explore more on these topicsPhiladelphia EaglesNFLUS sportscommentShareReuse this content

title: ‘I feel like I’m 21’: Joe Ingles on the NBA, life in Australia and 1,500 days without drinking | Basketball | The Guardian
description: The veteran is adjusting to living in Melbourne and playing in the NBL after 12 years spent on the North American basketball rollercoaster
Author: Jack Snape
Headline: The veteran is adjusting to living in Melbourne and playing in the NBL after 12 years spent on the North American basketball rollercoaster
Content: ‘I think it is a bit of a culture thing in Australia. When you catch up with your mates, you grab a beer or a coffee,’ Joe Ingles says as he returns to play in the NBL.Photograph: Daniel Pockett/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreen‘I think it is a bit of a culture thing in Australia. When you catch up with your mates, you grab a beer or a coffee,’ Joe Ingles says as he returns to play in the NBL.Photograph: Daniel Pockett/Getty ImagesBasketball‘I feel like I’m 21’: Joe Ingles on the NBA, life in Australia and 1,500 days without drinkingThe veteran is adjusting to living in Melbourne and playing in the NBL after 12 years spent on the North American basketball rollercoasterJack SnapeTue 20 Oct 2026 10.00 EDTLast modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 19.12 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBasketballer Joe Ingles appears as the archetype of the Australian larrikin. There is one box, however, he no longer ticks. The 39-year-old gave up alcohol in 2022 after suffering a serious knee injury, and he has now gone more than 1,500 days without drinking.“Stopping – that part of it – during rehab was very easy,” he says from Melbourne, after moving back to the NBL following 12 seasons in the NBA. At that point, it was just one aspect of aiding his recovery. Like staying healthy and avoiding junk food.Ben Simmons’ NBA comeback derailed after tearing achilles tendon in practiceRead more“I even had made a joke with my [Milwaukee] Bucks teammates at the time of, ‘Oh, when I play my first game, I’ll have a beer with you guys,’ whatever. I played my first game and I was just like, ‘eh’.”“My rehab was like 10 and something months. You go that long without a drink, and you’re, ‘Oh, do I really need this?’”His wife, Renae, a former Australian netballer and now coach and businesswoman,expressed pride about the couple’s milestoneon Instagram this week, and highlighted how “uncomfortable” it made people around them feel.Her husband has found it an adjustment as he came to terms with life back home. “I think it is a bit of a culture thing in Australia. When you catch up with your mates, you grab a beer or a coffee, really, they’re the two options,” he says, adding he has not ultimately found it hard to resist.View image in fullscreenJoe Ingles has quickly found his feet while playing with Melbourne United on his return to the NBL.Photograph: Daniel Pockett/Getty Images“After a certain amount of time, you don’t even think about it any more. It’s like you deleted Instagram and didn’t use it for a few months, you would just completely move on with your life and you wouldn’t even think about it any more, so we don’t even think about it. It’s not even a question, I think it’s more funny now that people will try and explain to us why they are drinking instead of just enjoy their night.”The couple and their three children are now adjusting to Melbourne after 12 years on the NBA rollercoaster. Ingles would typically travel for more than 40 road games each year, and he played for four different teams over his final five seasons. He has started the season for Melbourne United well, even if the highly fancied team is yet to fully gel.Despite being so far away, Ingles still watches the NBA, which gets under way this week. “I’ll be sitting there on Amazon watching just like you, and I’ll be just as intrigued,” he says. “I sit here and I read the same articles you do.”OnBen Simmons’ cruel Achilles injurythis week, Ingles is “shattered for him” and says it will be up to the former No 1 draft pick where his career goes now. “Selfishly for Australia, we want him to play for the Boomers. We’d love to see him in the NBL. I think the fans would love to see him. But what is he, two days since injury? There’s a lot of water to go under the bridge before those decisions even become a thing. I just wish him all the best.”On Josh Giddey’s situation in Chicago, Ingles believes a winning record will mean more than any individual statistics. On young big Rocco Zikarsky, likely to play big minutes in the second-tier G-League, Ingles thinks the 20-year-old could push for court time with the Timberwolves.Of the 10 Australians in the NBA this season (including Kyrie Irving in Dallas), Ingles believes Atlanta centre Jock Landale and Los Angeles Lakers wing Matisse Thybulle might make the biggest impression.View image in fullscreenJoe Ingles has backed Matisse Thybulle to have play a critical role for the Los Angeles Lakers during the 2026-27 NBA season.Photograph: Ben Liebenberg/AP“For [Landale] going back to the same team, a lot of the same players, same coach, don’t underestimate how good that feels,” Ingles says. “He was a free agent, they’ve wanted him back,they’ve paid him handsomely, and he’s going to have a really big role in that team.“Then the other one to me is Matisse, I’m selfishly a massive Matisse fan. The guys they’ve got on that team. Everyone knows Luka [Dončić] and Austin [Reaves] offensively, but defensively, they need a little bit of help out there and Matisse is that perfect guy.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionIngles turned 39 this month, and is signed to a two-year deal with Melbourne United. Across seven games he is averaging an efficient 11 points per game, with four assists and four rebounds.Although the veteran had to postpone his conversation with the Guardian by a day due to the need for treatment, he is adamant his body is feeling good. “I feel like I’m fucking 21 all right, so put that at the top of your article,” he says with a smile.As a late bloomer who became one of the NBA’s best role players, Ingles earned respect for his combination of outside shooting, secondary ball-handling and basketball nous, as well as a competitive edge. The combination of his laidback demeanour with a sharp, mocking tongue appeared very Australian, though it often rubbed American opponents the wrong way.Top talent and big money: is Australian basketball heading into a golden age? | Jack SnapeRead moreOff the court though, Ingles comes across as considered and diplomatic. Amid a growing schism about the role of betting in sports, San Antonio phenomenon Victor Wembanyama announced during the NBA off-season he wouldnever accept gambling money, even as LeBron James inked an endorsement deal with prediction market Polymarket.Ingles says sports betting is a “tricky one”, given sporting entities’ need for revenue, as well as the impact of increases in betting and integrity risks. Ingles was in the NBA when Jontay Porter was banned for life fordisclosing confidential information to sports bettors and wagering on games.“I don’t know where I sit necessarily on that,” he says. “Do I love chucking five bucks on a horse? Yeah, it’s a bit of fun with my mates. Do I live and die by betting on whatever it is? Absolutely not.“Everyone makes their own decisions with different things and people and politics they support and we can all have our opinions on things, we don’t have to agree.“But obviously, me and you can sit here and have a healthy conversation, debate about it, and both go off, and maybe we don’t agree in the end, but we’ve both put our points forward.”Explore more on these topicsBasketballAustralia sportUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: NBA 2026-27 season predictions: A Knicks repeat and LeBron’s villain arc  | NBA | The Guardian
description: Our writers give their verdicts on the new season, which tips off Tuesday. Can the Spurs or Thunder thwart a New York repeat? And which youngster will make the superstar leap?
Author: Lee Escobedo
Headline: Our writers give their verdicts on the new season, which tips off Tuesday. Can the Spurs or Thunder thwart a New York repeat? And which youngster will make the superstar leap?
Content: Lebron James, Victor Webanyama and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander will play big parts in this NBA season.Composite: Guardian Pictures (via Getty)View image in fullscreenLebron James, Victor Webanyama and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander will play big parts in this NBA season.Composite: Guardian Pictures (via Getty)NBANBA 2026-27 season predictions: A Knicks repeat and LeBron’s villain arcOur writers give their verdicts on the new season, which tips off Tuesday. Who will claim the title? And which youngster will make the superstar leap?Claire de Lune,Lee Escobedo,Bryan Armen Graham,Andrew LawrenceandOwen LewisTue 20 Oct 2026 05.00 EDTLast modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 13.01 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleWhat I’m most looking forward to …Seeing all the fruits borne of an incredible summer of player movement.It feels like three years ago that Giannis Antetokounmpo was traded to the Heat, because since then,Jaylen Brown and LeBron James went to the 76ers, and a ton of other deck chairs were reshuffled. This is the most intriguing NBA opening week in eons.Claire de LuneWashington and Utah clawing their way out of the doldrums. Both have been in perpetual poverty for almost half a decade. Both now surround young cores of switchy, two-way wings with playoff-tested veterans like Anthony Davis and Jaren Jackson Jr.Lee EscobedoThe NBA’s great chemistry experiment.After a summer in which Antetokounmpo landed in Miami and LeBron and Brown somehow wound up together in Philadelphia, the league feels like someone hit the reset button. Whether any of these hastily assembled superteams can actually function together is another question entirely. I’m particularly interested in how quickly the novelty wears off and the finger-pointing begins.Bryan Armen GrahamCan I be a homer and pickda Bulls? It appears they have their own generational Caleb – Caleb Wilson – to match the dynamic Bears quarterback, and the North Carolina prospect has looked like a draft steal since falling to fourth overall. Mix in the free-agent signing of Norman Powell (a veteran tough guy who expands his offensive range each year) and the addition of Tiago Splitter (a Gregg Popovich disciple who spurred Portland to a surprising playoff campaign last year), and these young Bulls sure look ready to run again.Andrew LawrenceA healthy Indiana Pacers team.I watched a lot of Pacers games last season, convinced they’d still be a playoff team as Tyrese Haliburton recovered from a torn Achilles – their magical run to the NBA finals in 2025 was very much a team effort – only to realize in dismay how Haliburton was not only the team’s beating heart, but the engine of their offense. Now Hali is back, Myles Turner is out, Ivica Zubac and Kelly Oubre Jr are in, and I am glued to my couch with a big bucket of popcorn.Owen LewisLeBron’s time with the 76ers will be …Irrelevant to his legacy.For all the hand-wringing and consternation about what will or won’t happen for LeBron and the 76ers in his tenure there, it’s ultimately a moot point. The (presumably) last stop of his storied career is a coda on what will likely go down as the greatest career in the history of the sport. Another ring would just be a cherry on top.CDLKawhi Leonard: a hero’s complicated return to the Toronto RaptorsRead moreNot how he imagined.Joel Embiid had the unmitigated gall to announce he’s“against the concept of sacrificing”. This leaves five starters with All-Star appetites fighting over one ball. Recent champions won with a legible hierarchy, a pecking order that settles crunch time and dictates the counter when defenses load up. Tyrese Maxey, coming off a career-high 28.3 points a game, belongs atop the pile. He and VJ Edgecombe will pay most for its absence.LEA magnificent circus.Philadelphia have spent more than four decades searching for the combination that will deliver another NBA championship, and now they’ve turned to a 41-year-old billionaire who wouldapparently rather be in New York. There will be spectacular nights, inevitable injuries, endless debates about load management and probably a fewhelicopter-related controversies. Whether any of it adds up to a championship is almost beside the point. The Sixers have become the most fascinating reality show in American sports.BAGEventful.It already has been with him choppering back and forth from New York and media and fans scrambling to trace leaks about Embiid’s perceived commitment back to his camp, reportedly keen to arrange a reunion with Davis. If the Sixers’ Monstar team don’t jump out to an early lead in the East – or worse, falter in Eagles-like fashion – the King risks courting the most intense scrutiny of his basketball career from a fanbase that’s already on his case before he’s even played.ALCounting on the health of a 41-year-old LeBron and Embiid’s knees – to this point proven to have the durability of Cheez-Its – seems unwise. This team is bursting at the seams with star power, but it’d be easy for injuries and a clunky fit to yank them off the rails before they ever find their rhythm. Still, in the name of delusional optimism and LeBron’s career so far:thrilling and tumultuous.OLYoung player to make the superstar leap …View image in fullscreenDylan Harper is set to be a force for the Spurs this season.Photograph: Ross D Franklin/APDylan Harperwas arguably San Antonio’s most consistent player in their finals run last season …as a rookie.The sky is the limit for this insanely talented NBA nepo baby, and I think we see him as an All-Star and maybe even a fringe All-NBA player this year.CDLAlex Sarr’sfield-goal percentage jumped from 39.4% as a rookie to 48.2% last season. He reads the short roll like a guard and attacks closeouts off the dribble. Trae Young should make him a premier lob threat for the Wizards. RememberClint Capela shooting 64.6% off Young’s passes in 2020-21? The next frontier is individual defense beyond his two blocks a night, and he now apprentices himself to Davis, a five-time All-Defensive selection.LEAmen Thompson.The athletic gifts have never been in question. What makes the Rockets star so tantalizing is the possibility that his offensive game catches up with the havoc he already wreaks defensively. Houston have enough talent around him that he won’t have to manufacture everything himself, but there’s a version of Thompson who becomes the Rockets’ most important player on both ends of the floor. That version may arrive sooner than anyone expects.BAGOne could argue thatCade Cunninghamis already there after leading Detroit to the east’s top seed and otherwise filling out the box score like he did last year. This year, though, I think is when more fans recognize that the Oklahoma State product belongs in the same conversation with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Nikola Jokić et al. And if all the work Cunningham put in during the offseason to improve his three-point accuracy bears fruit, the Pistons could have a serious MVP contender on their roster.ALCooper Flagg. The 19-year-old spent last season playing the point on an undermanned Mavericks squad, but nonetheless put up 51-, 49-, 45-, and 42-point nights. With Kyrie Irving back from a long layoff with a torn ACL, Flagg stands to excel even further with a talented second option beside him in his sophomore season.OLThis season’s villain arc will be supplied by…Victor Wembanyamaseems quite content to take on the role as villain. It was a cumbersome fit, at first: it’s hard to seem like the bad guy when you’re playing chess with fans in the park and bemoaningthe trappings of sports betting. But fresh off a finals drubbing, Wembanyama enters this season on a mission: destroy everything in his path.CDLThe owners, an American oligarchy in miniature.Miriam Adelson bankrolled Donald Trump, whocredited her family, from the Knesset rostrum, with shaping his Israel policy. Steve Ballmer is serving ayearlong suspension for cap circumvention.I traced Robert Pera’s Ubiquiti radiosto Russia’s drone war on Ukraine. Josh Kushner, brother of Trump’s son-in-law,agreed to buy the Lakers.My own team’s ownerbuilt a petty panopticon.LEThe NBA’s gambling partners.Forget Draymond Green. The league’s real villains are turning every possession into a speculative asset. With gambling scandals mounting, the NBA isalready restricting certain betswhile its partners flood broadcasts with advertising. The actual basketball seems to be becoming a sideshow.BAGLeBron,see above.ALDoesn’tJames Dolanalready have this title locked up? The Knicks got to enjoy their championship for all of five minutes before Dolan announced that theywould not go into the second apron.Mitchell Robinson is now a Celtic. Karl-Anthony Townsis unhappy with extension talks. Dolanis renting out Madison Square Garden to raise money for a GOP candidate. Somebody find this man a competent PR manager, or a moral compass.OLMost Valuable PlayerSpeaking ofVictor Wembanyama, the MVP is his to lose. Barring a significant injury, I don’t see anyone swiping either this award or defensive player of the year from him. He’s fresh off a surprise finals berth, finished high in the MVP voting last year, and is rapidly making his case for the best player in the association.CDLVictor Wembanyamais inevitable.I raised the alarmlast year. The defensive player of the year adds MVP this season, a double nobody has managed since Giannis in 2020. No athlete since prime LeBron has bent physics like this. A man who thinks in myths and epics watched his own late turnover decide Game 2 of the finals, then watched the Knicks celebrate on his floor. He’ll spend 82 games proving he never chokes again.LEVictor Wembanyama.This one feels overdue before it’s even happened. Jokić remains the best offensive player alive, Luka Dončić can bend entire defenses to his will and Gilgeous-Alexander has made ruthless efficiency his brand. But Wemby is becoming something none of them can match: a one-man defensive system who can also score 30 a night. Voter fatigue should take care of the rest.BAGGiannis Antetokounmpo.Not only is he healthy, but he’s got a squad around him that fits his lunch-pail personality and an organization that is seriously committed to winning championships. With shooters around him and Bam Adebayo on the floor for shutdown defense and an offensive spark, there’s no telling how far Giannis can take the Heat – but any sort of rebound for this perennial play-in contender is likely to come down to his vintage brilliance.ALVictor Wembanyama. It’s less that Jokić can’t win his fourth MVP or Dončić his first with especially potent offensive wizardry (voters are notoriously unlikely to give out three MVPs in a row, which rules out Gilgeous-Alexander) than that I think Wemby’s unparalleled and ever-improving two-way superpowers will prove impossible to ignore.OLEastern Conference playoff teamsKnicks, 76ers, Celtics, Heat, Pacers, Raptors, Pistons, Cavaliers.CDLKnicks, Pacers, Hawks, Heat, 76ers, Pistons, Cavaliers, Raptors.LEKnicks, Celtics, Cavaliers, 76ers, Pacers, Pistons, Hawks, Heat.BAGBulls, Pistons, Celtics, Cavaliers, Knicks, 76ers, Heat, Hawks.ALPistons, Knicks, Celtics, Pacers, Cavaliers, 76ers, Raptors, Hawks (sorry, Heat fans, I don’t trust Giannis’s health).OLWestern Conference playoff teamsSpurs, Thunder, Lakers, Timberwolves, Nuggets, Rockets, Trail Blazers, Warriors.CDLSpurs, Thunder, Timberwolves, Nuggets, Lakers, Rockets, Trail Blazers, Jazz (!).LEThunder, Spurs, Nuggets, Lakers, Rockets, Timberwolves, Warriors, Mavericks.BAGThunder, Spurs, Nuggets, Rockets, Timberwolves, Pelicans, Warriors, Mavericks.ALThunder, Spurs, Rockets, Nuggets, Lakers, Timberwolves, Trail Blazers, Mavericks.OLEastern Conference finalsKnicks over 76ers.CDLKnicks over PacersLECeltics over Knicks.BAGKnicks over 76ers.ALPacers over Knicks.OLWestern Conference finalsSpurs over Thunder.CDLTimberwolves over SpursLEThunder over Spurs.BAGSpurs over Thunder.ALThunder over Spurs.OLNBA finalsView image in fullscreenAre we heading for another Knicks title?Photograph: Ronald Cortes/Getty ImagesSpurs 4-3 Knicks.It’s been the better part of a decade since we got an NBA finals rematch, and we’re due. While the path out of the East will be tremendously more difficult this year, and the Spurs’ path out of the West won’t exactly be a picnic, either, the safe bet feels like a rematch of last year’s finals. However, I do suspect a different outcome: with a deep playoff run of experience under San Antonio’s belt, and Wemby fully embracing his villain arc (and the weightroom), I think this is the year he adds the first of several finals MVPs to his ever-expanding trophy cabinet.CDLKnicks 4-2 Timberwolves.New York hadthe best offensive ratingandthe best defensive ratingof last postseason. The Knicks swept the conference semifinals and finals on the way to 13 straight wins, the second-longest run in a single postseason. Then they handed Wembanyama’s Spurs a gentleman’s sweep. Wipe away those tears and accept the defending champions. Minnesota spent the offseason building a deep, polymorphous roster around Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball, and I respect it.All five Knicks starters return, though, and in this league, continuity is king. Remember, with Jalen Brunson, anything is possible.LEThunder 4-2 Celtics.The NBA’s fixation on parity has made picking a champion feel like throwing darts blindfolded, but Oklahoma City remain the closest thing the league has to a sustainable dynasty. Gilgeous-Alexander is still in his prime, the supporting cast is absurdly deep and last season’s disappointment should provide ample motivation. Boston’s experience carries them through the East, but the Thunder’s athleticism and defensive versatility ultimately prove too much. The league gets another champion from a small market – ending an unprecedented run of eight different champions in eight seasons – and the rest of the NBA gets another reminder that continuity might actually matter.BAGSpurs 4-1 Knicks.The Spurs get revenge and beat the Knicks, kicking off a new championship rivalry for the era. But this time, instead of riding Wemby till he runs out of gas or deferring to De’Aaron Fox in the clutch, Mitch Johnson puts the onus on Harper – who makes the leap from supersub to superstar to finals MVP. He and Wemby emerge as the Shaq and Kobe of their day, with San Antonio fans holding their breath in hopes that their egos remain modest and keep this dynasty in the making from blowing up in Kawhi-like fashion.ALThunder 4-3 Pacers.Nobody repeats in the parity era, but the Thunder got close. With injuries to two vital offensive contributors,they still wrestled their biggest rival to a tight Game 7in the Western Conference finals. I think they exact revenge over the Spurs this year. The retooled and revitalized Pacers will be the last team standing after a bloodbath in the East. In the finals, they’ll provide a sequel to their magnetic series from 2025, only Haliburton will be healthy for Game 7. We’ll just get the same result.OLExplore more on these topicsNBABasketballUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Google cloud failure hits millions as UK courts and banks knocked offline | Revolut | The Guardian
description: Services restored for most users, but power fault stalled hearings and left Revolut, Lloyds and HSBC customers unable to pay or move money
Author: Kalyeena Makortoff
Headline: Services restored for most users, but power fault stalled hearings and left Revolut, Lloyds and HSBC customers unable to pay or move money
Content: The Revolut outage could be linked to issues with Google’s cloud services.Photograph: Mateusz Słodkowski/Zuma Press Wire/Rex/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenThe Revolut outage could be linked to issues with Google’s cloud services.Photograph: Mateusz Słodkowski/Zuma Press Wire/Rex/ShutterstockRevolutGoogle cloud failure hits millions as UK courts and banks knocked offlineServices restored for most users, but power fault stalled hearings and left Revolut, Lloyds and HSBC customers unable to pay or move moneyKalyeena MakortoffandJulia KolleweTue 20 Oct 2026 05.45 EDTLast modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 18.58 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAn outage at Google’s cloud services in the UK has caused widespread disruption, hitting courts and leaving millions of customers unable to access or send cash at banks including Lloyds, HSBC andRevolut.Google blamed a “power event” for the failure at its London-based Cloud computing operations on Tuesday, which affected its “europe-west2-b zone”.The US tech company said services were starting to come back online as of 1pm London time, and were back online for most customers by 3pm, but not before critical financial transactions and legal proceedings were disrupted.That included the video system used by defendants, lawyers and other parties to attend court hearings remotely across England and Wales, which failed to work throughout the morning.The issue was believed to have delayed several hearings, as the system is often used for defendants who are in custody but need to attend court.Meanwhile, bank customers at high street lenders and leading digital bank Revolut were left in limbo as services including card payments, cash withdrawals and transfers were disrupted.By 5pm most Revolut services were still marked on its website as having problems, with only six out of 27 services listed, including support chat and internal transfers, said to be working.The City regulator, the Financial Conduct Authority, confirmed it was in touch with Google and seeking more information about the outage. The Bank of England’s Prudential Regulation Authority is also understood to be speaking with the tech firm.Halifax, owned by Lloyds Bank, said on X that some of its customers had been unable to log in via the app and online.Revolut said its app was down because of a “service disruption” affecting several services, but insisted that customers’ funds and data were safe. The outage was affecting new and current customers, hitting its sign-up, sign-in, card payment, transfer, ATM withdrawal and cryptocurrency services.In a statement, Revolut said: “We are currently experiencing a service disruption affecting multiple services. We can confirm that all our customers’ money and data are safe. We’ve been working to fix the issue since it was identified this morning and apologise to anyone affected and for any inconvenience caused.”A spokesperson for Lloyds originally said that customers were having issues with “certain online services” on Tuesday morning but that they were aware of “similar issues affecting other organisations”. By the afternoon, the banking group issued an update saying: “We understand the root issues have been resolved, so we expect to [have] all our services back to normal soon.”HSBC customers had also been complaining online that they were struggling to access their accounts. A spokesperson for the bank said: “Our services have returned to normal following earlier access issues. We continue to monitor the situation closely and thank customers for their patience.”This outage will be the first major test for the FCA and the Bank of England since the City watchdogs werehanded powers to regulate Google and other rival servicesthat have been supplying “critical” cloud services to UK financial firms this summer.Their response is already facing scrutiny by the influential Treasury committee of MPs, whose chair Meg Hillier wrote to the regulators asking for details about how they reacted and a sense of the total impact on the UK financial system. Hillier has asked for an initial response by 4 November.The property portal Rightmove was also reportedly affected by the Google cloud outage, and NewsThump, the satire and spoof news website, was struggling to load. Reports suggested Royal Mail and DPD had also suffered disruption.Google said: “We will publish an analysis of this incident once we have completed our internal investigation. We thank you for your patience while we’re working on resolving the issue.”An FCA spokesperson said:“We are aware of the incident affecting services provided by Google and are engaging with them and affected firms to understand the impact.“People need to be able to access their money and make payments, so we expect firms to fix issues quickly, keep their customers informed and ensure no one is left out of pocket.”Explore more on these topicsRevolutBankingGoogleFinancial sectornewsShareReuse this content

title: The dangers of letting tech billionaires shape our world | Technology | The Guardian
description: As SpaceX impacts Ukraine and AI-generated music divides artists and fans, critics are asking what happens when technology has too much control over our lives
Author: Blake Montgomery
Headline: As SpaceX impacts Ukraine and AI-generated music divides artists and fans, critics are asking what happens when technology has too much control over our lives
Content: The Tesla CEO and X owner, Elon Musk, attends the VivaTech conference in Paris on 16 June 2023.Photograph: Gonzalo Fuentes/ReutersView image in fullscreenThe Tesla CEO and X owner, Elon Musk, attends the VivaTech conference in Paris on 16 June 2023.Photograph: Gonzalo Fuentes/ReutersTechScape newsletterTechnologyThe dangers of letting tech billionaires shape our worldAs SpaceX impacts Ukraine and AI-generated music divides artists and fans, critics are asking what happens when technology has too much control over our livesThis was originally published in TechScape, a newsletter about how technology shapes our lives.Sign up to receive it hereBlake MontgomeryTue 20 Oct 2026 10.31 EDTLast modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 12.45 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleHello, and welcome to TechScape. I’m Blake Montgomery, US tech editor at the Guardian, writing to you while sitting in front of Roy Lichtenstein’s monumental Drowning Girl,on view in New York City. Today in tech, we’re discussing the perils of Elon Musk’s one-man global infrastructure, AI-generated music and a Guardian AI conference in Paris.Elon Musk’s orbital ownershipElon Musk’s SpaceX is the single largest satellite operator in the world, larger than any government space bureau. The life-threatening consequences of that dominance and centralization of power are on full display. One man is in charge of global, vital infrastructure, which is thumbing the scales in the war on Ukraine.SpaceX’s internet service was throttled in Ukraine amid a series of devastating attacks by Russia last week, leaving the country extremely vulnerable. The US government controls StarShield, the satellite internet service produced by SpaceXSI for the Pentagon, which is what Ukraine relies on. Objects moving faster than 100mph (161km/h) – drones, the centerpiece of Ukraine’s counteroffensive – lost connectivity. The sudden restrictions Tuesday evening led tothe failure of several Ukrainian combat missions. Russian drones fly at nearly 200mph (329km/h), so Ukrainian interceptor drones can’t catch them without Starlink, and no alternative is as yet viable. In response, the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, warned “people will die.”The cutoff comes alongside Donald Trump’s mercurial souring onUkraine. Pressured domestically by the high price of diesel and upcoming midterm elections, the US president has eased sanctions on Russia, and Zelenskyy has said US intelligence agencies on several occasions in recent days didn’t warn Ukraine of incoming missile attacks, as they usually do. Musk has denied his own involvement in StarShield’s malfunctioning, writing, “This is not under SpaceX control.”Reutersreported that the request to throttle the service in Ukraine came from the White House. Responding to the claim, Trump said: “I don’t know if it was anybody because it wasn’t me, and I don’t think it was Elon. And from what I understand, it’s the same as it’s always been.” The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, said “no one at the White House ordered anyone to slow down the internet.”Read more:What is Starshield, SpaceX’s military-grade Starlink system, and how will its restriction affect Ukraine?Musk’s denial has been met with skepticism given his close ties with the administration. It is impossible to disentangle him andSpaceXfrom the Trump administration. He has realigned himself with the White House in recent months, patching up his explosive feud with the president from a year ago and appearing with Trump at major events. Musk has been appointed to a Pentagon commission on the future of war and has given hundreds of millions of dollars to conservative Republican candidates.Musk has also personally ordered the restriction of Starlink service in Ukraine before. In 2022, SpaceX cut off Starlink – not StarShield – service during a Ukrainian counteroffensive in the regions of Kherson and Donetsk. He refused Ukraine’s request to extend connectivity to Crimea the same year.One tech tycoon’s political leanings are determining the tides of war between two sovereign nations. Musk’s alliance with the White House implicates him in the pressure campaign against Ukraine to end the war with Russia, likely via surrender.Artists and fans reckon with AI-generated musicView image in fullscreen‘If somebody does a totally AI-generated song where all they did was prompt something, then I think that’s their thing. But who am I to say what’s standard and what’s not?’Photograph: Krisanapong Detraphiphat/Getty ImagesIn recent weeks, notable musicians have confronted the growing presence of AI-generated music, saying they are open to it but wary, even boosters like the singer and producerGrimes, former paramour of Musk and mother to three of his 14 children.Fans, by contrast, are voting with millions of streams against artifice in music. Songs and albums harkening back to analog instrumentation are dominating the Billboard charts, no futurism wanted.Both A$AP Rocky, rapper and partner to Rihanna, and Grimes took the same position: I accept AI-generated music, but I don’t make it.“I prefer to do things myself, practically,” A$AP Rocky toldBillboard. “If somebody does a totally AI-generated song where all they did was prompt something, then I think that’s their thing. But who am I to say what’s standard and what’s not? I’m just doing me out here, and I’m doing my music practically – the right way.”Grimes, one of my own favorite musicians, has begun promoting her first new album in six years, Psy Opera, which she described tothe Paris Reviewas capturing the “emotion of being thrust into the future”.Stereogumdescribed the album as “AI-inspired but not AI-generated”, citing Grimes’s own insistence that her team of 70 be credited rather than reduced to machines.Grimes offered a free license of her own voice to AI enthusiasts to make what they would three years ago. That she declined to generate her own music indicates that, even to a futurist like her, AI-generated music is lacking, similar to Rocky’s stance.I have also found myself listening to an AI-generated song, Bomboclat Wallahi, brought to my attention viafrenetic, overstimulatingvideoson Instagram. Despite the song’s comical sonic maximalism, it lacks any staying power. Listening to it the day after I first heard it left no impression, similar to the way low-quality food leaves me hungry again just a few hours after eating. “Slop” is still the best word to describe AI-made content.In contrast to artists’ nuanced stances, fans are making their position on tech-made music clear: they don’t want it.Billboard’s chartsof the most popular albums and charts of the past week showcase a preference for music without obvious modification. Songs and albums that feature a simple voice-and-guitar arrangement are dominating. On the Top 200 album charts, most of the Top 10 albums foreground a singer over analog instrumentation – Olivia Rodrigo’s you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love, Ella Langley’s Dandelion, Olivia Dean’s The Art of Loving, Taylor Swift’s The Life of a Showgirl, Noah Kahan’s The Great Divide and Stick Season, and Morgan Wallen’s I’m the Problem. In the Hot 100 singles chart, the top four songs bear the same sonic signatures: Swift’s Patient Zero, Langley’s Choosin’ Texas, Stella Lefty’s Boston, Wallen’s Been by Now.Incredibly, The Beatles’ Rubber Soul, released in 1965, also makes an appearance at No 4 on last week’s Billboard rankings. Some listeners want to return to a time when producing music with artificial intelligence wasn’t even an option.Be more human: how to resist the creep of AIView image in fullscreen‘We decide that we want to be more human.’Photograph: Marcela Barsse/Getty ImagesMy colleague Robert Booth reports from the Hacking Big Tech conference, a Guardian conference in Paris:As the Paris Streets erupted with protest and violence on Saturday, a parallel radicalism was on display at the Hacking Big Tech conference organised by the French media organisation Mediapart in conjunction with the Guardian. Amid the contributions from experts in military AI and how to fight against datacentres, a theme emerged about how people might respond to the tech wave: be more human.The writer Naomi Klein told the audience that the technology companies intend AI to be used as an “everything app and also as a truth machine”. This, she said, was “very clearly a fascist idea, to centralise knowledge, to standardise what intelligence is”.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toTechScapeA weekly dive in to how technology is shaping our livesEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAt a rare tech conference not addressed by representatives of tech companies, Klein painted a bleak AI-driven future in which there is “going to be more resource scarcity, there’s going to be more people who have no role in the economy and need to be contained and surveilled”.A response was available, she said: “We decide that we want to be more human.”Humour was another answer. German Salazar, a Chilean activist campaigning to save water in his native country in the face of a wave of AI datacentres, showed how his community had set up a human chatbot to encourage people to prompt less and save water. The idea was simple: a team, ranging from children to town elders, offered human responses to chatbot queries from anywhere in the world for a day. If you want an image of a dog doing yoga, one of them will paint it for you. Want to know what love is? A human will tell you it is “the wish of someone else to be happy”.There were 2,300 requests for images, 135 for dating advice and one for the meaning of life.Read more:AI threatens democracy. But we are not powerless: here’s how to fight backThe wider TechScapeTool and target: US law enforcement grapple with AI-enabled terrorism and anti-tech extremismApple unveils new smart home devices that showcase upgraded Siri AICompanies rushed in on AI.
